lines.jp: ───逃げこんだ廃屋に満ちた、焦燥感と苦しげな息遣いが、中に敗残兵の収容所じみた様相をもたらしていた───
lines.en: --The desperation and ragged breathing filling the abandoned house where they had taken refuge made it resemble a camp for defeated soldiers.--

lines.jp: 皆一様に荒い息で、肩を壊れる寸前の鞴の様に上下させているが、呼吸の乱れはしつこく残り、なかなか去ってくれようとしない。これまで知らざる恐怖との邂逅が皆の体力気力を鑿を当てたように奪っていた。
lines.en: Everyone panted alike, shoulders pumping like bellows about to split. Their breathing clung raggedly on and would not settle. The encounter with an unknown terror had taken a chisel to body and spirit alike.

lines.jp: 乱れた呼吸で肺と喉が炉の中のように灼けて、肌一面が天火に炙られたかのよう、なのに夥しく伝う汗は、身体を損ねてしまいそうなくらい悪く冷たい。
lines.en: Disordered breaths burned their lungs and throats like a furnace, and their skin felt baked by an oven. Yet the sweat streaming over them was so cold and foul it seemed liable to make them ill.

lines.jp: ───大海蛇から逃れた、といってもその場しのぎに過ぎないという事実が、それぞれの肩に重く粘くへばりついていた。
lines.en: --The knowledge that they had escaped the great sea serpent only for the moment clung to every shoulder, heavy and viscous.--

lines.jp:
裏街道の悪党どもをせせら笑い、立ちはだかるものがあれば鉄火と暴力で薙ぎ倒し、時には裏をかいて逃げ道を掠め取ってきた信天翁号の面子にして、初めて遭遇する劫初の恐怖だった。
　性質としてはシサム・キサラが出くわした大怪魚悪婁に近しいが、あれより遙かに陰湿で貪欲で凶猛で残酷で、邪神のような邪悪ささえ纏うていたことを、遭遇した者全員肌感覚で、そしてそれより深い本能で感じ取っていた。
lines.en:
The crew of the Albatross had sneered at criminals along the back roads, mowed down anything in their way with gunfire and violence, and sometimes stolen an escape by outwitting their enemies. Yet this was the first primordial terror they had ever faced. 
In nature it resembled Akuro, the giant monstrous fish Sisam and Kisara had encountered, but it was vastly more insidious, greedy, ferocious, and cruel, cloaked even in the evil of a dark god. Everyone who had met it sensed that upon their skin and in instincts deeper still.

lines.jp: ───太古から生き続けてきた、人間より古い、理解を拒む根源的恐怖。
lines.en: --A primal terror older than humanity, alive since ancient times and refusing all understanding.

lines.jp: あれは、そういうモノだ。
lines.en: That was what it was.

lines.jp: 「あれが……あんなのが、この島の動物達の最後の生き残りかよ……」
lines.en: That... That thing is the last surviving animal on this island...?

lines.jp:
下級水夫達からの無言の糾弾と非難の目に耐えかねて、角隅にクロを連れてしゃがみこむ朔屋の前に、航海士の編み上げの長靴が床の軋みも酷薄に立ちはだかる。
　胸ぐら掴み取られて顔面蹴球の球と腫れ上がるまで殴打の嵐か、さもなくば長靴の爪先で肋を全て粉砕するまで蹴り込まれるか、いずれにせよ仕置きと痛めつけられることは間違いなく、朔屋は長靴とミニスカートの間の太腿を鑑賞する気力はおろか、目を上げることさえできなかった。
lines.en:
Unable to endure the junior sailors' silent accusation, Naomasa had taken Kuro and crouched in a corner. Now a Chief Mate's laced boot stood before him, making the floor creak with cruel promise.
 She might seize his collar and beat his face round as a football, or drive the boot's toe into his ribs until every one shattered. Either way, punishment and pain were certain. Naomasa lacked even the spirit to admire the thigh between boot and miniskirt, much less raise his eyes.

lines.jp: 航海士が身じろぐ気配に、のろのろとクロを背中にかいこむ。どうせこの白子の少女とて、程度の差はあっても朔屋と同様の目に遭わされるだろうが、それを目の当たりにするのはあまりに辛く、順番が後回しになれば恐怖もより募る。
lines.en: At the slightest movement from the navigator, he slowly drew Kuro behind his back. The albino girl would probably receive the same treatment as he did, if perhaps to a different degree. But seeing it would be too painful, and if her turn came later, the waiting would only deepen her fear.

lines.jp:
朔屋もクロも怯えきっていたから、自分達へ叩きつけられめりこんでくる拳足がとりあえずはないのにも気づかず俯いたままだったから、航海士はしまいに焦れてどん、と脚を踏み鳴らした。
　それだけでも朔屋の睾丸は痛いほど体内に縮み上がったし、クロなどは一つ大きく身を震わせてから、朔屋の背中に額を押し当ていやいやとぐずぐず涙したほど。
lines.en:
Naomasa and Kuro were so frightened that they remained bowed, never noticing that no fists or feet were presently striking them. At last the navigator lost patience and stamped one foot with a bang. 
That alone made Naomasa's testicles contract painfully into his body. Kuro gave a great start, pressed her forehead against his back, shook her head, and whimpered through tears.

lines.jp: 大海蛇は大海蛇として、今は眼前の女の方が間近に迫った大いなる危機、恐ろしくて仕方なかったが、無視を決めこんだところで状況が打開されるわけもなく、その上とうとう焦れきったか、航海士が太腿のガンベルトから回転式弾倉抜き払い、撃鉄まで起こしてきたので、泡を食って顔を上げる。
lines.en: The great sea serpent was one thing, but the woman before him now seemed the more immediate mortal danger. He was terrified of her, yet pretending she did not exist would not change matters. Finally, apparently out of patience, the navigator drew the revolver from the gun belt at her thigh and even cocked the hammer. Naomasa looked up in alarm.

lines.jp: これで自分の頭をぶち抜いてケリをつけろと拳銃を押しつけられたわけでもなく、腹をかき切れと船員ナイフを握らされたわけでもなく、航海士が差し出してきていたのは、ごしゃごしゃとした布の堆積、いや、イルカやオットセイの肌の質感、鼻先をついたのはゴム張りのきつい匂い、潜水夫が身に着けるような、ウェットスーツだった。
lines.en: She had not pressed the pistol into his hand and ordered him to finish matters by blowing his brains out, nor given him a sailor's knife and told him to cut open his belly. What she held out was a tangled heap of fabric--no, something with the texture of dolphin or seal skin. The sharp smell of rubber struck his nose. It was a wetsuit of the kind a diver might wear.

lines.jp:
「……島の根っこの部分が気になったんでね。
　後で潜ってみるつもりだった。
　もうそんな必要もないわけだけど」
lines.en:
...I was curious about the underside of the island. 
I planned to dive down and investigate later. 
Not that there's any need for that now.

lines.jp: 「で、こいつを着て、あの化け物の前を横切ってこい、と」
lines.en: So I put this on, and walk across the monster's path. Is that it?

lines.jp:
樹脂製のウェットスーツ、絶縁の。
　朔屋にしては呑みこみよく理解して、浮かべた笑みは安堵からではない、もっと捨て鉢な、殴りつけてやりたくなるように荒んでいた。実際つい拳を握りしめたほどである。
lines.en:
A resin wetsuit. An insulator. 
Naomasa understood surprisingly quickly. The smile that rose to his face came not from relief but from a bleak recklessness irritating enough to make someone want to punch him. In fact, the navigator's fist tightened.

lines.jp: 「あのさ。素直に俺を生贄にしてさ、俺があれに食われちゃってる隙にみんなが走ったほうが早いんじゃないの？」
lines.en: You know, wouldn't it be quicker to offer me up as a sacrifice and have everyone run while that thing eats me?

lines.jp:
「あたしらを信じろ、朔屋。
　確かにあんたとクロを囮にはするけど、
　あんたらを見捨てたり、
　見殺しにはしない」
lines.en:
Trust us, Sakuya. 
We are using you and Kuro as bait, that's true. 
But we won't abandon you, 
and we won't leave you to die.

lines.jp:
「はっはっは、俺も他人の事は言えないが、
　あんたらを信じろと？」
lines.en:
Hahaha! I'm hardly one to talk about others, 
but you expect me to trust you people?

lines.jp:
「べったべたと疑い深い奴だなあ。
　じゃあこう言えばいいか？」
lines.en:
What a stubbornly suspicious bastard. 
Would you prefer if I put it like this?

lines.jp: 「あんたらを囮に使って、それでようやく勝ちの目も出てくるんだ。あんたらがもしやられちまったら、あたしら、万に一つの目もなくなる」
lines.en: Only by using you two as bait do we have any chance of winning. If that thing gets you, even our one-in-ten-thousand chance disappears.

lines.jp:
「後はあの淫獣に、
　全員後をレイプされてお終いさぁ」
lines.en:
Then that obscene beast catches every last one of us 
and has its way with us. The end.

lines.jp:
「一蓮托生、ってわけだ。
　どうだ、少しは道理が見えたかい？」
lines.en:
We're all in the same boat. 
There. Does that make a little more sense?

lines.jp:
「一応もっともらしくは聞こえるけど。
　なんか俺、騙されてない？」
lines.en:
It sounds plausible, at least. 
But aren't I being tricked somehow?

lines.jp:
「大丈夫。お前みたいに馬鹿が過ぎると、
　騙す騙されるどころじゃなくなる。
　下手すると騙そうとしたほうが、
　阿呆みたいなしっぺ返しを喰らう事になる」
lines.en:
Don't worry. When someone is as stupid as you are, 
it stops being a question of fooling or being fooled. 
If anything, the person trying to trick you 
risks some idiotic kind of retaliation.

lines.jp:
「そろそろええな？
　こうしてる間にもヤツぁどこをぬたくり通ってくるのかわからんのだ」
lines.en:
Are you about done? 
While we stand here talking, there's no telling where that thing might come slithering through.

lines.jp: 「それに朔屋、そのスーツなら、たといあの化け物にカマをほじられようとも、少しは防いでくれるだろう」
lines.en: Besides, Sakuya, that suit ought to protect you a little even if the monster tries to violate you.

lines.jp: 「行っておいで、朔屋」
lines.en: Off you go, Sakuya.

lines.jp: 「せいぜい派手に囮をやってねぇ」
lines.en: Make yourself as flashy a decoy as you can.

lines.jp: 「朔屋さん、ファイトー！」
lines.en: You can do it, Sakuya!

lines.jp: 「僕らのお尻を護る為、頑張れーっ」
lines.en: Fight hard to protect our backsides!

lines.jp:
（簡単に言ってくれるよなあ。
　俺ぁ駆けっこはビリから数えた方が早かッたっつうのに……）
lines.en:
(Easy for them to say. 
When I ran races, you could count my place faster from the back...)

lines.jp:
「クロ……行こうか。
　どうにも納得はいかなくっても、
　世の中ってのは───」
lines.en:
Kuro... Shall we go? 
Even when we can't accept it, 
the world...

lines.jp: 「……そんなものでしかないみたいだ」
lines.en: ...Seems to be nothing more than that.

lines.jp:
「……なっとくが、いかないのが、
　よのなか……」
lines.en:
The world... is something 
you can't accept...

lines.jp: 朔屋に手を取られて、逆らいもせず、というより引かれるままのクロ、何事かを考えていた。一心に考えて考えて、クロが辿り着く答えは、多分。彼女にとっては苦い味になるだろう。
lines.en: Naomasa took Kuro's hand. She did not resist, but merely followed where he pulled, thinking about something. She thought and thought with all her heart. The answer Kuro reached would probably taste bitter to her.

lines.jp: 「やっぱり……クロは」
lines.en: After all... Kuro is...

lines.jp: クロの内心にどんな思いが去来しているのか、言葉として表せなくともその想いの味は朔屋にも伝わって、舌に苦い。
lines.en: Even if Kuro could not express the thoughts passing through her heart in words, their flavor reached Naomasa and lay bitter upon his tongue.

lines.jp:
まともな装備と物資に乏しい信天翁号の事である。単純に大人二人分を用意できなかっただけの事かも知れない。
　それでも───
lines.en:
The Albatross was notoriously short of proper equipment and supplies. Perhaps they simply could not provide two adult-sized suits. 
Even so--

lines.jp:
ウェットスーツは二つ有ったけれど、大人用の物は一つ。残りは、クロでも着用できそうな程に小さい物。
　偶然と言ってしまえばそれまで。
　だがそれがしつこく朔屋の心に引っかかったし、クロの内部が少しずつ変容しつつあるのも気にかかる。
lines.en:
There were two wetsuits, but only one was made for an adult. The other was small enough for Kuro to wear. 
It might have been pure coincidence. 
Still, it nagged persistently at Naomasa, as did the gradual change taking place inside Kuro.

lines.jp: 愚かで力足らずではあったけれど、それでもクロは彼女なりに『善き人生』を希求して、前に歩む力と為していた。
lines.en: She was foolish and weak, yet in her own way Kuro still sought a "good life" and used that desire as the strength to move forward.

lines.jp: クロ───朔屋には、この白子の少女がノアの方舟から放たれた鴉の、呪われて彷徨い続けた成れの果てなのだ、という事が完全に納得されたわけではない。
lines.en: Kuro--Naomasa had not entirely accepted that this albino girl was what remained of a raven released from Noah's Ark after wandering beneath a curse without end.

lines.jp: クロ───時に神がかった操船能力を発揮し近づき難い相を垣間見せる時があったとしても、朔屋にとって彼女は、ちっぽけで痩せッぽちで、そして健気な、クロ、だった。
lines.en: Kuro--though at times she displayed an almost divine mastery of the ship and showed a face none could approach, to Naomasa she was still tiny, skinny, brave little Kuro.

lines.jp:
その未成熟な身体を抱きもした。
　共に泣いた事もあった。
lines.en:
He had held her immature body in his arms. 
They had cried together.

lines.jp: その少女の中から、抜け落ち流れ去っていく心がある、その後から現れつつある哀しい理解がある。
lines.en: But something was draining from the girl's heart, and in its place arose a sorrowful understanding.

lines.jp: 世界は残酷な物でしかないという事実。
lines.en: The fact that the world was nothing but cruel.

lines.jp:
クロがそれを完全に受け入れてしまった時、彼女がどう変わってしまうのか───
　朔屋には、その結末が、あの大海蛇と同じくらいに恐ろしいことのように感じられてならず───
lines.en:
When Kuro accepted that completely, how would she change? 
To Naomasa, the answer felt as frightening as the great sea serpent itself--

lines.jp:
木造建築の合間、通路と通路が合流してちょっとした広場のような間隙を為している地点で、大海蛇は縮まった蛭のようにじっとして、身じろぎもせずに。
　だが動かずにいるとはいえ、この前を横切って老人の海図があるという建物に向かうのは並大抵の覚悟では足らず、朔屋とクロは失禁寸前であった。
lines.en:
At a gap between wooden buildings where several passages joined into a small plaza, the great sea serpent lay motionless, contracted like a leech. 
Yet stillness did not make crossing before it toward the building said to contain the old man's chart any less terrifying. Naomasa and Kuro were both on the verge of wetting themselves.

lines.jp:
それでも進むしか他に道はなく、互いの存在をよすがとして、そろそろと歩み始める。
　眠っているのかなんなのか、動かない大海蛇の前を極力跫音と息を忍ばせて、横切っていく。慣れないスーツが動きを阻害し、ゴムの擦れる響きが二人の耳には万雷ほどにも巨大に響く。
lines.en:
They had no choice but to continue. Drawing courage from one another's presence, they began creeping forward. 
Whether it was asleep or something else, the serpent did not move. They crossed before it while suppressing their footsteps and breath as much as possible. The unfamiliar suits hindered their movement, and the sound of rubbing rubber thundered in their ears.
Shhh--

lines.jp: 「しぃー……っ」
lines.en: Shhh...

lines.jp:
低くお互いの息遣いを鎮め合い、一歩、一歩、踏みしめた足を抜いて、差しこむように進めて、また一歩。
　溜まらない時間がのろのろと流れ、僅か数十米の移動が万里の長城の踏破ほどにも二人の神経と体力を磨り減らし、目が回る、目が眩む、息が苦しい、心臓は内側から胸骨と肌をぶち破ってしまいそうに激しく乱打して、もう一歩も歩けない、今度こそ立ち止まってしまう、そんな際を破れかぶれの気力でか、臆病故の生き汚さでか、辛うじて乗り越えて、ようやく、遂に、とうとう、やっと、広場の端、海図の建物への通路の入口まで後数歩、まで至る。
lines.en:
They hushed one another's breathing, lifted each planted foot, slid it forward--and took one more step.
 Unendurable time crawled past. Crossing a few dozen meters wore down nerve and sinew as though they were walking the Great Wall: their heads spun, their sight dimmed, breath caught, hearts battered as though to break through breastbone and skin. Each time they reached the brink of stopping, whether desperate will or a coward's tenacious love of life carried them across it. At last--finally, at long last--only a few steps remained between them and the passage to the chart building.

lines.jp: ここまで来たなら、たとえ大海蛇が不意に動き出したとしても、通路には逃げこめると、朔屋はそろそろと背後に目をやったのが、傷となった。それも死に繋がる傷だ。
lines.en: They had come far enough that even if the serpent moved, they could flee into the passage. Naomasa slowly glanced behind him--and that glance became a wound. A mortal one.

lines.jp: 振り返れば大海蛇は今だ静止したままで、ほっと気が緩んだ、途端に足下の板の継ぎ目に爪先を取られ───
lines.en: The great sea serpent remained perfectly still when he looked back. Relief loosened his body--and his toe caught in the joint between two boards.
Oof!?

lines.jp: 蹴躓いた弾みで、長靴の隙間に差してあったあの望遠鏡が弾け飛び、がらんと床に落ちて転がっていった響きが巨大だった。しかも、大海蛇の鼻先から程遠からぬ位置に。
lines.en: As he stumbled, the telescope tucked into his boot flew free. It struck the floor and rolled with a deafening clatter, stopping not far from the great sea serpent's snout.

lines.jp: 「あ、だめ、それ朔屋さんの……っ」
lines.en: Oh, no! That's Sakuya's...

lines.jp: 「ほっとけ、そんなの今は……っ」
lines.en: Leave it! Not now...

lines.jp: 「大丈夫、まだへいき……んしょ」
lines.en: It's all right. Still safe... Up we go.

lines.jp: よせばいいのに、望遠鏡を拾い上げるクロ、だがなんと幸運なことか、大海蛇は気づいた様子はない。
lines.en: Though she should have left it alone, Kuro picked up the telescope. By astonishing good fortune, the great sea serpent showed no sign of noticing.

lines.jp: ───かに見えて。
lines.en: Or so it appeared.

lines.jp: クロが背を向ける隙を待ち構えていたのだろう、青黒い、卑猥で、汚怪で、そして貪欲で凶猛な生命体の、動き出して、その様、クロと朔屋達、温血の生き物とはあまりに隔たっている故に、どこか神さびている、とも言えた。
lines.en: Perhaps it had been waiting for Kuro to turn her back. The blue-black, obscene, filthy, greedy, ferocious life-form stirred. Its movement was so unlike Kuro and Naomasa--so alien to warm-blooded life--that it seemed almost numinous.

lines.jp:
だが、戦き見守るうちに、クロの背後に鎌首がゆっくりともたげられるを目にしてしまった朔屋にとっては、神も悪魔もあったものかで、胸掻きむしり、地団駄踏み、焦燥感に気が狂いそうに、いや狂う、今狂う、それくらい恐ろしいのに。
　実際、限度を越えた恐ろしさが、朔屋の神経の接続を狂わせたのだろう。
lines.en:
But Naomasa saw its head slowly rise behind Kuro as he watched in terror. Gods and demons meant nothing then. He wanted to claw his chest and stamp his feet; the desperation threatened to drive him mad--no, he was going mad now. It was that terrifying. 
In fact, the fear must have exceeded all limits and scrambled the connections in Naomasa's nerves.

lines.jp:
あれ？　と朔屋は、首を傾げていた。
　なぜ自分の身体が前に進んでいるのだ？
　何故クロに向けて手を伸ばして───
　何故かは判らないけれど、何故だって良いではないか、むざむざ彼女を見捨てるよりは！　一度勢いが付いてしまえば、朔屋は自分の足が思っていたよりは随分と増しに走ってくれる事が有り難かった。
　疾走の勢いを利して、クロの腕を捕まえて、
lines.en:
Huh? Naomasa tilted his head.
 Why was his body moving forward?
 Why was he reaching toward Kuro--
 He did not know. It did not matter. Anything was better than standing by while she was taken! Once momentum carried him forward, he could only be grateful that his legs ran far better than he had ever credited them.
 He used the force of his charge to catch Kuro by the arm.

lines.jp:
「……駄目だったみたいだ。
　走れえええっっ！」
lines.en:
...I guess it didn't work. 
Ruuuun!

lines.jp:
知っていた筈なのに、無我夢中の勢いがその軽さを失念させた、藁の束を抜いたような頼りなさで、勢い余って牛蒡抜きにクロの身体、宙に放り投げてしまいそうになる。掴む手は為さず、遊園地の遊具のように一回転、振り回して勢いをやっと殺して、横抱きに腕の中に収めて、一目散だ。
　望遠鏡はスーツの首から背中に押しこんだ、ごわごわするがもう落としてもいられない。
lines.en:
Though he knew how light she was, the frenzy made him forget. Her body came free as feebly as pulling a bundle of straw, and his momentum nearly hurled her into the air. He did not release her, but swung her in a full circle like an amusement-park ride until their momentum finally died, caught her sideways in his arms, and ran for his life. 
He shoved the telescope down the back of his suit through the collar. It was stiff and uncomfortable, but he could not afford to drop it again.

lines.jp:
「お、おろして。クロ走れる。
　一人で走れる───」
lines.en:
P-put Kuro down. Kuro can run. 
Kuro can run by herself--

lines.jp:
「無理だって言うの！　お前さんの足じゃ、
　走ったって追いつかれる」
lines.en:
No, you can't! With those legs, 
it'll catch you even if you run!

lines.jp:
それに、何もクロを助けたいどうこう以前に、今さら彼女を下ろす為に一々足を留めていたら、それだけでも追いつかれてしまいそう。背後で身じろぎして、巨体が動き出す気配に板敷きの通りが軋む、音だけで竦み上がりそう、振り向いてなどいられない、走る、朔屋が屠殺場から逃げ出した鶏のように懸命に駆ける。
　クロが軽すぎてかえってバランスが取れない。落とすまいと強く抱きしめているだけでも壊してしまいそう。肋同士がぶつかって軋む。痛い。でも構っていられない今は。
lines.en:
Besides, quite apart from any desire to save Kuro, stopping now simply to put her down might be enough for the beast to catch them. Behind him, the plank street creaked beneath the motion of its enormous body. The sound alone nearly froze him. He could not look back. Naomasa ran with all his strength, like a chicken escaped from the slaughterhouse. 
Kuro was so light that carrying her actually threw off his balance. Even holding her tightly enough not to drop her felt as if it might break her. Their ribs collided and groaned. It hurt, but that no longer mattered.

lines.jp: 「……朔屋さんに、迷惑……」
lines.en: ...Kuro is... a burden to Sakuya...

lines.jp:
「迷惑かけられる相手がいるだけ、
　幸せと思えっ」
lines.en:
Consider yourself lucky 
you have somebody to burden!

lines.jp: こんな状況、死にもの狂いの状況、物語や伝説中にしか登場し得ないような怪物に、この今の代、今の世の中になって追いかけられていると言うのは、一体なんだ？　悪夢か？　誰かの仕掛けた質の悪い冗談か？　クロが思い詰めたように呟いたが、細かく相手していられる余裕などなく、つい怒鳴り返したが、それ故に朔屋の実感であったろう。
lines.en: What was this situation? In the present day, in the modern world, they were being chased for their lives by a monster that should have existed only in stories and legends. Was it a nightmare? Some vile joke? Kuro murmured in despair, but Naomasa had no time to answer her gently and shouted back. For that very reason, however, the words were probably his honest feeling.

lines.jp:
「しあわせなの……？　そんなのが？
　じゃあクロは……。
　ずっと誰かに、迷惑をかけていても、
　それでしあわせ……？」
lines.en:
Is that... happiness? Something like that? 
Then Kuro... 
can keep burdening somebody forever, 
and be happy...?

lines.jp: 「当たり前だろうっ。迷惑がホントに厭なら相手にしなくなるよ、それでも付き合ってくれる奴が居るのは幸運な───あーもう、いいから黙ってつかまってろ、クロ！」
lines.en: Of course! If someone really hates the trouble, they'll stop dealing with you. You're lucky if they still stay with you-- Oh, enough! Just shut up and hold on, Kuro!

lines.jp: 朔屋に怒鳴られて、クロは意外な言葉を聞いたような、少し驚き目で腕の中から見上げれば青年は、雨粒と脂汗で顔をどろどろにして、なりふり構っていられない疾走に、口角からは涎、鼻水だって伸びて、頭は密着するスーツのお陰で変梃に丸くて。はっきり言ってしまえばとてもみっともなくて。
lines.en: Startled by his unexpected words, Kuro looked up from his arms. Naomasa's face was drenched in rain and clammy sweat. He ran too desperately to preserve any dignity, drool at the corner of his mouth, mucus trailing from his nose, and his head made oddly round by the clinging suit. To put it plainly, he looked utterly pathetic.

lines.jp:
けれどそれは全て自分の為なのだと知った時クロは───
　クロは恥じ入った。深く深く、今となっては懐かしいあの『船長の箱』に入ってしまいたくなるそれくらいに。それぐらい恥ずかしくて、自分が悪い、いけないものになってしまったような疚しさに襲われた。
lines.en:
But when Kuro realized all of it was for her--
she felt deeply ashamed, so deeply she wanted to crawl back inside the old "captain's box" that now seemed almost nostalgic. She felt embarrassed and guilty, as though she herself had become something bad and forbidden.

lines.jp:
何故なら少女は、朔屋という青年が、ここまで気取りも何もない、生のままの顔をさらけ出しているのが、自分を助けようと、自分のためにしてくれているのだと実感した時、無上の喜びに包まれてしまっていたから。
　この、体の底からぞわぞわと押し寄せて、喉にむず痒いくらいの感触は、きっと、嬉しい、そういうものなのだと。
lines.en:
For when she understood that Naomasa had exposed this raw, utterly unguarded face because he was trying to save her--doing all of it for her--Kuro found herself flooded with a joy beyond measure.
 The feeling tingled upward from the bottom of her body and tickled her throat. This must be what it meant to be happy.

lines.jp: クロが無言に唇を引き結び、朔屋の首筋に強くしがみついて胸板に顔押しつけるようにしたのは、青年の言葉にただ従ったからでなく、こんな時に嬉しいと感じてしまっている自分が恥ずかしくて、見られたくなかったからだったのだ。
lines.en: Kuro silently pressed her lips together, clung tightly around Naomasa's neck, and buried her face against his chest. She did so not merely because he had told her to hold on, but because she was ashamed of feeling happy at a time like this and did not want him to see.

lines.jp:
朔屋という一人の青年が、自分のためにこんなにも必死になってくれる事に、喉の底から突き上げてくるような歓びを、一瞬間だけど感じてしまって。
　もちろんクロはそれを恥じたし、いけない事だと後悔したし、その一瞬の歓びだけでもう充分とどこかで諦めていたし、それ以上の事は望まなかったのに。
lines.en:
For one instant, joy had surged from the bottom of her throat at the knowledge that one young man, Naomasa, would struggle so desperately for her sake. 
Of course Kuro was ashamed of it and regretted that it was wrong. Somewhere inside, she had already decided that single instant of joy was enough. She had wished for nothing more.

lines.jp:
……何処の天上の、どんなご本尊やら知らないが、狭量な奴もあったもの。強欲か色欲か、いかなる罪科に数え上げたかは定かならぬが、幸いの実のちょっと端っこを囓っただけのクロに罰をくれてよこしたとしか考えられなかった。
　よこした罰は、朔屋の足許に転がった缶殻の形に顕現した。
lines.en:
...Whatever object of worship sat in whatever heaven, it was a narrow-minded one. Whether it counted her offense as greed, lust, or some other sin was unclear, but it seemed to have punished Kuro merely for nibbling one corner of the fruit of happiness. 
That punishment manifested as an empty can rolling beneath Naomasa's feet.

lines.jp: クロを抱きかかえていた為に視界が及ばなかったし、背後には、粘つく体表に、雨粒を弾けさせる電気と充たされる事のない餓えを纏う大海蛇が肉迫していたし、朔屋は足許に目を配ってなどいられず───
lines.en: Because he carried Kuro, he could not see his feet. Behind him, the great sea serpent bore down, its sticky surface clad in rain-splitting electricity and hunger that could never be filled. Naomasa had no attention to spare for the ground--

lines.jp: クロもまた、朔屋の顔ばかりを見あげていたから。こういう時には、感謝の気持ちはちゃんと言葉にしないと伝わらないと知っていたから、朔屋に言おうとして。
lines.en: Kuro, too, had been looking only up at Naomasa's face. She knew gratitude had to be put properly into words or it would never reach him, so she tried to speak.

lines.jp:
「しゃべんなっ、舌を噛む、
　───って」
lines.en:
Don't talk! You'll bite your tongue--
Wait--

lines.jp: 「うおっ!?」
lines.en: Whoa!?

lines.jp: どれだけしっかりとしがみついていたつもりでも、クロの腕の力は、やはりどこまでも足りなくて、朔屋の身体伝いに、足許から響いた衝撃を聞いた時にはもう、もぎ離されてしまってあり───
lines.en: No matter how tightly she thought she had clung to him, Kuro's arms were still far too weak. By the time she felt the impact travel up from beneath Naomasa's feet, she had already been torn away.

lines.jp:
朔屋は抱えていた軽さが失せた事に、取り返しのつかない事態が見舞った事を知り、クロは自分の腕の、大事な者さえ捉まえていられない非力だったこと、今さらのように呆然となって。
　喪失感を二人に刻みこむように、世界の速度がこの瞬間、残酷な事に零に近づいた。
lines.en:
The disappearance of that light weight from his arms told Naomasa something irreparable had happened. Kuro stared in shock at the weakness of arms unable to hold on even to someone precious. 
As though to carve the sense of loss into them both, the speed of the world cruelly slowed almost to zero.

lines.jp:
ゆっくりと緩慢に、クロの身体が朔屋の腕の中から抜けていく。
　クロは朔屋の顔が、呆然と、それから悔恨の表情に歪んでいく、筋肉の動き一つ一つを眺めている。
lines.en:
With terrible slowness, Kuro's body slipped from Naomasa's arms. 
She watched every muscle in his face move, first into shock and then regret.

lines.jp: けれど、これだけお互いの動きが視えるのなら、判るのなら、と二人は互いに手を差し延べる───手が、指先が届く、触れ合う、絡み合う！
lines.en: Yet if they could see and understand one another's movements this clearly, they could still reach. Both stretched out a hand--their hands, their fingertips met, touched, entwined!

lines.jp:
───かに見えて。
　水の中に落ちていく貝殻に、手を差し入れて捕らえようとしてもどうしてもうまくいかない。指の前でするりと抜けていく。
　この時の二人のように、絡み合ったはずの指と指が、するりと抜けていく、離れていく。
lines.en:
Or so it appeared. 
Reach for a shell sinking through water, and somehow it always slips smoothly past your fingers. 
So it was with them. The fingers that should have intertwined slid apart and separated.

lines.jp:
もう一度試みる事も許されなかった。
　二人にその瞬間を引き延ばして味合わせてやりたかっただけ、と言いたげに世界の時間は巻き締まり、復調した。
lines.en:
They were not permitted a second attempt. 
As though the world had only wanted them to savor that prolonged instant, time wound tight again and resumed its course.

lines.jp: 朔屋は前のめりにクロを投げ出す形となっていたとはいえ、とすんと哀しいくらい軽い音で、少女が地に伏したのは、青年の前方、かなり離れた位置でそんなにも勢いが付いてしまっていたのか。
lines.en: Naomasa had pitched forward and flung Kuro ahead. Her body struck the ground with a sadly light sound, far in front of him. Had he truly been moving with that much force?

lines.jp: 「クロ、大丈夫かッ!?」
lines.en: Kuro! Are you all right!?

lines.jp:
「朔屋さん、立ってぇ……っ。
　逃げて───」
lines.en:
Sakuya, get up... 
Run--

lines.jp: クロは短い悲鳴をつまらせ顔を引き歪めたが、ぐっとこらえて朔屋へと手を差しのばす、が、腰から下は崩れたまま。恐怖と驚愕が立ち上がる力を奪っている。
lines.en: Kuro choked off a short cry and twisted her face in pain, but endured it and reached toward Naomasa. Below the waist, however, her body remained collapsed. Terror and shock had stolen the strength to stand.

lines.jp:
青年の背後には、獲物と認めて大海蛇の、その汚怪な雁首を蠕動させつつじり、じりと。
　怪物の巨体には一息に詰められない距離ではない。なのに様子を窺うように緩慢なのが、慎重さの表れというより、この怪生物の獲物を嬲る残忍性を示していた。
lines.en:
Behind the young man, the great sea serpent had recognized its prey. Its filthy head writhed as it crept steadily closer. 
With its enormous body, it could have closed the distance in an instant. Its slow approach seemed less cautious than a display of cruelty, a desire to torment its prey.

lines.jp:
「いいからまずお前だっ。
　逃げてくれ、頼むから……っ」
lines.en:
Forget me! You go first! 
Please, just run...

lines.jp:
「た、立てないクロ、あしが、腰が、
　いごかないよう……っ」
lines.en:
K-Kuro can't stand. Her legs, her waist... 
They won't move...

lines.jp: 「動くッ。大丈夫だっ。嵐を呼ぶ船長、それがクロだろうっ！　あの時も今も、身体だけはおんなじなんだから！」
lines.en: They will! You're all right! You're the captain who summons storms, aren't you? Your body is the same now as it was then!

lines.jp: 大海蛇はもう背後で狙いを定めているはず、このように絶縁のスーツを着こんでいても、顔の露出した肌には雨の日に高圧電線の鉄塔の下を通った時のような電気の刺激をぴりぴりと感じている。スーツは同時に、体腔に侵入させようという大海蛇の口吻を防いでくれるかも知れないけれど、あの巨躯ではのしかかられただけで全身の骨が砕けるだろう。
lines.en: The great sea serpent must already have taken aim behind him. Even through the insulating suit, the exposed skin of Naomasa's face prickled like walking beneath a high-voltage pylon on a rainy day. The suit might also protect him from the serpent's invasive method of feeding, but a creature of that size could shatter every bone in his body merely by crushing him beneath it.

lines.jp:
恐怖は当然のようにある。恐ろしくないわけがない。けれど朔屋には、この時ここでクロまでこの怪生物に屠られてしまうのが、とてつもなく無念に感じられたのだ。
　それは幾らか、信天翁号の船員達への反感も手伝っていた。自分達をこの危地に送りこんだ者への。
lines.en:
Of course he was afraid. How could he not be? But at that moment, Naomasa found the thought of Kuro being slaughtered by the monster unbearably bitter. 
Some of that feeling arose from resentment toward the Albatross crew who had sent them into this danger.

lines.jp: 「ほら、行くんだ、クロ!!」
lines.en: Come on! Go, Kuro!

lines.jp:
背後の怪生物を刺激してしまう事にもなろうが、知った事かと朔屋は、むらむらと滾る無念、反感を籠めて、拳をどんと板敷きの通りに叩きつける。
　朔屋の剣幕と、板伝いに拳の衝動伝ったか、クロの背筋にびしりと筋が通って、彼女を咄嗟に立ち上がらせた。
　となれば後は勢いが付けばいいと朔屋は顔の半分を口にして───
lines.en:
It might provoke the creature behind him, but Naomasa no longer cared. He drove his fist against the planked street with a bang, packing the blow with all his seething bitterness and resentment.
 Whether from Naomasa's ferocity or the shock transmitted through the boards, Kuro's spine snapped straight and she sprang instinctively to her feet.
 All she needed now was momentum. Naomasa opened his mouth so wide it seemed to split his face in half--

lines.jp: 「おがあああああ～～～～！」
lines.en: Ogaaaaaaaah!

lines.jp: 寝つきの悪い子供を脅しつける物怪声で、顔つきで、クロはひっと顔を引きつけると、反射的に飛び退いた、その一歩が弾みとなって、二歩、三歩と踏み出すうちに歩度が伸び、速さも増して、板敷きの通りの奥へ。その、スーツによって細さばかりが強調された背中を見送って、朔屋は。
lines.en: With the face and monstrous howl of something frightening a sleepless child, he made Kuro recoil with a squeak. That first backward step provided momentum for a second and third. Her strides lengthened, her speed increased, and she ran down the wooden street. Naomasa watched the suit emphasize the thinness of her retreating back.

lines.jp:
（あああ……やっちゃったよ俺。
　何かっこつけてんの俺。俺、ここで死ぬの？
　やだよ、怖いよ、そんなの、怖い───）
lines.en:
(Oh no... I actually did it. 
Why did I try to act so noble? Am I going to die here? 
I don't want to. I'm scared. That's terrifying--)

lines.jp:
少女を逃げ延びさせてから敢然と、あるいは逍遥と、朔屋は結末を受け入れるのにどちらの態度もとらなかった。
　クロが逃れたと見るや恐怖に眸濁らせ、ばたばた手足で通りの床材を叩き、そのくせ立って逃げ出す事も怖くて出来ない、ただ怖い怖いと譫言のように呟き続ける情けなさを完全に露呈させ、不様極まりない最期を遂げようとしていた。
　大海蛇がその雁首を収縮させているのも、朔屋の醜態を楽しんでいるかのよう。
lines.en:
After allowing the girl to escape, Naomasa met his end neither boldly nor serenely. 
The moment Kuro was safely away, terror clouded his eyes. He slapped his arms and legs against the street, yet was too frightened even to stand and flee. He exposed himself completely, muttering "I'm scared" like a delirious child as he approached a thoroughly undignified death. 
The serpent contracted its head as though enjoying Naomasa's disgrace.

lines.jp: 朔屋はがちがちいう音を聞いた。勝手に鳴りだした、恐怖に震えた歯列が鳴らすスタッカートだ。
lines.en: Naomasa heard a rapid clacking. It was the staccato of his own teeth, chattering uncontrollably with fear.

lines.jp: 朔屋はとたとたいう音を聞いた。こちらの音は朔屋を別な意味で恐怖させた。なぜにと言って、そのとたとた、跫音は朔屋へと近づいていたから。せっかく一度は遠ざけたつもりだったのに。
lines.en: Then Naomasa heard a soft patter. That sound frightened him in a different way, because the footsteps were approaching him. He had gone to all that trouble to send their owner away.

lines.jp: （なんで戻って来ちゃうかなあこいつは）
lines.en: (Why did she have to come back?)

lines.jp: 朔屋の顔は恐怖によって、涙と鼻水と脂汗でどろどろぐちゃぐちゃ、それはもう目を背けたくなるほどの有り様だったが、クロも似たようなものだった。啜り泣き、しゃくりあげて、ちょっと口をしっかり閉じていれば、ちょっと眼をぱっちり澄ましていれば、不健康そうな隈に目を瞑れば、それなりに可憐な貌立ちが、もう台無しの、朔屋とクロで何もこんなところで不様の顔見本を競わせなくともよかろうにというほど。
lines.en: Fear had reduced Naomasa's face to a revolting mess of tears, mucus, and cold sweat, but Kuro looked little better. She sniffled and sobbed, ruining features that could have been reasonably lovely if only she kept her mouth closed, opened her eyes clearly, and one overlooked the unhealthy shadows beneath them. There was no need for Naomasa and Kuro to stage a contest in wretched expressions here of all places.

lines.jp:
「やっぱり、できない、朔屋さん置いてくの、
　クロはやだよぉっ、だって、そしたらきっと、クロは、どうやても、幸せ、なくなる」
lines.en:
Kuro can't do it. She can't leave Sakuya. 
Kuro doesn't want to, because then, somehow, Kuro knows she could never be happy again.

lines.jp: 涙で湿った声、腫れぼったい瞼、夜鳴きする赤子をもっと歪めたような表情。そして全身覆うスーツからはきゅっきゅっとゴムが擦れる奇妙な音立てて、この時のクロはもう悲惨なくらいにみっともなく、もしかすると普段の朔屋なら、こんな形相で近づかれたならついうっかり蹴り倒してしまったかも知れない。それなのにこの今は、どうしてこんなにも嬉しいのか。
lines.en: Her voice was damp with tears, her eyelids swollen, and her face more contorted than a baby crying in the night. The suit covering her body squeaked oddly as its rubber rubbed together. Kuro looked disastrously pathetic. Ordinarily, Naomasa might have kicked her down by accident if she approached him with a face like that. Why, then, was he so happy now?

lines.jp: 朔屋の側まで、大海蛇に目がいってしまわないように硬い目つきで戻ってきてから、クロはぺたんと膝をつき、とすんと腰を落として、青年の前で項垂れて。
lines.en: She returned to Naomasa's side with her gaze held rigidly ahead so that she would not look at the serpent. Then Kuro dropped to her knees, sat flat before the young man, and bowed her head.

lines.jp:
「もう。どうせ。
　ここでクロ、死んじゃったって。
　別にね、もういいかなって」
lines.en:
It's all right now. Even if... 
Kuro dies here... 
Kuro thinks that might be okay.

lines.jp:
だって、自分のために。
　こんなにも必死に、変梃な顔になってまで。
　喚いて叫んで、怒ってくれる人がいる。
　それが判ったから。
　その誰かが朔屋だと判ったから。
lines.en:
Because, for her sake, 
someone had struggled this desperately, even making such a ridiculous face. 
Someone had shouted, screamed, and grown angry for her. 
She understood that now. 
And she understood that person was Naomasa.

lines.jp:
「おおう……そんなヤケ言うなよう。
　俺、クロに目の前でおっ死なれるなんていやだぞ……」
lines.en:
Hey... Don't give up like that. 
I don't want to watch you die right in front of me...

lines.jp:
「って、それはお前もおんなじ、なのか？
　俺にくたばられるのが厭だから？
　だからのこのこ戻って来ちまったってか？」
lines.en:
Wait, is it the same for you? 
You came wandering back because you don't want me to die? 
Is that it?

lines.jp: あい、とクロは素直に頷いて。
lines.en: Yes, Kuro replied with an honest nod.

lines.jp: ……二人の頭上で、大海蛇はさて、どちらからにしようかなと言わんばかりに鎌首を左右に巡らせている。そんな怪獣をクロは、怖々と見あげて、ちらりと見ただけでおぞましさに身を縮こまらせて、でもどこか観念したように、
lines.en: ...Above their heads, the great sea serpent turned its raised head from side to side, as if choosing which one to eat first. Kuro looked fearfully up at the monster and shrank from its horror after only a glance. Yet with a strange air of acceptance, she said,

lines.jp:
「あー……さいごまで、いっしょかぁ。
　これ、たぶんしあわせなんだ」
lines.en:
Ah... Together until the end. 
This is probably happiness.

lines.jp: えへへ、と思いもかけず素敵な貝殻でも拾ったように、赤い眸に喜色を浮かべて。
lines.en: She gave a shy giggle, her red eyes bright with joy as though she had unexpectedly found a beautiful seashell.

lines.jp: 大海蛇は、食前の下処理のつもりで、何度か眼下の二人に電撃を送ってみたのだけれど、他の獲物のようには麻痺してくれないので、ちょっと考えこむ。
lines.en: The great sea serpent sent several electric shocks at the pair below, apparently intending to prepare them before feeding. When they failed to become paralyzed like its other prey, it paused to consider.

lines.jp:
「クロ、ほしかったのは、きっとこれ。
　みんなに、認めてもらうの、もういいや」
lines.en:
This must be what Kuro wanted. 
Kuro doesn't care about everyone accepting her anymore.

lines.jp: そして、うん、と一つこっくり頷いて、クロは理解を得ていた。諦観、と言うべきか。分別、と言うべきか。結局自分が望んで得られるものは限られているのだと。でも、それが青年であるのなら、それになんの不足があるのだと───クロは理解して、諦めてそして、大いに満足していた。
lines.en: Kuro gave one deep nod. She had reached an understanding--or perhaps resignation, or good sense. What she could wish for and actually obtain would always be limited. But if what she could have was this young man, what more did she lack? Kuro understood, relinquished the rest, and felt utterly content.

lines.jp: さて大海蛇君は、先ほどまでぴちぴち活きが良かった獲物達が、なんだかすっかり大人しくなっているのに不審の念を抱いていた。死んだふりだろうか。大海蛇の好みというのは、生に必死にしがみつこうとする獲物を追いかけ弱らせ、さんざんに嬲って然る後に孔に尖端を挿入してから、消化酵素で肉や内臓を溶かし尽くして吸いあげる事だが、少しは厭がってくれないと趣に欠ける。この獲物二体が捕食者を前にして逃げる風も見せないのは、あるいは病んでいるのだろうか。
lines.en: The great sea serpent, meanwhile, grew suspicious that the lively prey from moments earlier had become completely docile. Were they pretending to be dead? It preferred to chase victims clinging desperately to life, exhaust and torment them, and only then consume them through its invasive feeding method. Prey that showed no resistance lacked appeal. Perhaps these two were diseased.

lines.jp: が、何時まで逡巡していてもしかたがない。発電しうる最大の電撃をくらわせれば、少しくらい丈夫な皮膚を持っていたとてどうにもなるまい。大海蛇、畜勢に入り───
lines.en: Still, it could not hesitate forever. The strongest electric shock it could generate should overcome even somewhat resilient skin. The great sea serpent began gathering its charge--

lines.jp:
「なにやったって、怒らりるもの。
　なら、なにもしないで、朔屋さんと」
lines.en:
No matter what Kuro does, everyone gets angry. 
So Kuro would rather do nothing, and stay with Sakuya.

lines.jp: 最期にクロは、身を乗りだし、それは嬉しそうに莞爾し、朔屋の首を抱きよせて、唇と唇を重ねようとした。好きな人同士がこうする事を知っていたから。
lines.en: At the end, Kuro leaned forward with a radiant, delighted smile. She wrapped her arms around Naomasa's neck and moved to place her lips against his, because she knew that people who loved one another did so.

lines.jp:
「お、おい、よせやいこんな時に、
　いや、ま、いっかー……」
lines.en:
H-hey, not at a time like this! 
Though... Well, why not...

lines.jp: 朔屋も、先ほどまであれほど躍起となってクロを逃そうとしていたけれど、もうどうでも良くなって、白状してしまえばクロが戻ってきたのが何やら嬉しくて、疲れきっていたのも手伝って、青年は、そしてクロは、極めて自堕落に、後の事は大海蛇の好きにしろと、いい加減に適当に生命を、投げ捨てた。
lines.en: Until moments earlier, Naomasa had been desperate to make Kuro escape. Now he no longer cared. Truthfully, he was somehow happy she had returned, and exhaustion helped wear down his will. Naomasa and Kuro surrendered their lives with extraordinary abandon, leaving whatever came next to the serpent.

lines.jp:
───さて。
　身を捨ててこそ浮かぶ瀬もあれ、とは言うたものだが。
　二人の心境とは遠く隔たるところであろう。
　
　しかし───
lines.en:
--Now then. 
It is said that only by casting away one's life can one rise to safety, 
though that was far removed from what the two actually felt. 

And yet--

lines.jp: 朔屋とクロが覚悟、と言うか、もう色々とどうでもいいという投げ遣りな気分に陥ったその時。
lines.en: At the moment Naomasa and Kuro reached what resembled resolve--or simply stopped caring about anything--

lines.jp:
覚悟めいた、気持ちといっても、望んでいたぞと微笑む魂などである筈はなく、二人はただただその瞬間がさっさと到来してくれよと。もう痛いだろうとか苦しいだろうとか、想像するのも厭で面倒くさくて。
　こういう厭なものを待ち受ける、鈍速化した時間の中で朔屋が、鼻の奥に刺してくるの感じる匂いは、大概消毒綿の刺激臭で、きっとこれは幼き日注射に泣いた頃の記憶なのだろう、それにしてもまだなのか、クロなんかまた震え始めてる、と苛立ちさえ小生意気に覚えた始めた時に、風切り音だ。
lines.en:
Their feeling resembled resignation, but these were hardly souls smiling because they had wanted this end. They only wished the moment would hurry up and arrive. Even imagining the pain and suffering had become tiresome.
 As Naomasa waited inside that slowed time, the sharp smell of antiseptic cotton pricked the back of his nose--perhaps a memory of crying before childhood injections. Was it not over yet? Kuro had begun trembling again. He had just started to feel a petulant irritation when something cut through the air.

lines.jp:
と、耳に認めて、一拍ほど間があったろうか───叩きつけられた塊！
　頭上からだったし、重く荒々しい威力、を即座に連想させたし、朔屋もクロも共に身構えたのだこれがきっと最大の電撃あるいは体当たりだから今は音だけだけれどその次に体をすごい痛みが襲う何処にくる腕か頭かお腹か背中かどれだけ辛いのか歯を食いしばるかそれとも堪えない方が一瞬ですむのか───
　襲いかかるであろう痛苦に身構えた二人なのだが、しかしこの時二人をまず叩いたのは、大海蛇の電撃でもその体躯を利した圧撃でもなく、音の一撃だ、ギュッと握って圧縮したのが弾けるような。
lines.en:
After his ears recognized the sound, perhaps a single beat passed--then some mass struck! 
It came from overhead with a force that immediately suggested something heavy and violent. Naomasa and Kuro both braced themselves. Surely this was its greatest electric shock or a bodily charge. There was only sound now, but pain would follow--where would it strike, arm, head, stomach, back, how terrible would it be, should they clench their teeth or would failing to resist make it end faster? 
But what struck them first was neither electricity nor the crushing force of the serpent's body. It was a blow of sound, as though something compressed in a tight fist had burst free.

lines.jp: それは、二人と大海蛇が位置する区画、その頭上にさしかかる木造建築群を、正体不明の威力が爆砕した轟音。あまりの衝撃に朔屋とクロの体が横滑りしたほどで、二人とも完全に虚を衝かれ、周囲の状況と認識の接続が断たれた。猫の鼻先で思い切り手を打ち鳴らした時、動きが止まってしまう生理作用と同じだが、大海蛇の方さえ、瞬間に凝結していた。二人に狙い定めた形のまま。この生物の感覚知覚がどのような機構を取っているのか定かではないが、こういった捕食者も、獲物を襲うその瞬間には無防備になる、こちらもまさにその虚を衝かれた。
lines.en: An unknown force blasted apart the wooden buildings above the section where the pair and the serpent stood. The impact sent Naomasa and Kuro sliding sideways, so completely surprised that awareness and surroundings broke apart. It was the reflex that freezes a cat when someone claps before its nose. Even the great sea serpent froze in the instant, still poised to strike. Whatever mechanism governed its senses, this predator too became defenseless at the moment it attacked--and the blast caught that very opening.

lines.jp: ごん、と朔屋達のすぐ脇に落ちた、木造家屋の梁材の太さに朔屋は震え上がった。ごんと落ちて、余韻を残して震えている。これがもし脳天に落ちてきたら、中身を撒き散らして悶死していただろうの想像の方が、大海蛇に襲われる瞬間より判りやすく朔屋に活を入れて、立ち上がらせて、もちろん忘れずクロの手を引っ張って。
lines.en: A wooden beam struck the ground beside them with a heavy thud. Its thickness made Naomasa tremble. It fell and continued vibrating with the impact. The clear thought that it would have scattered the contents of his skull and killed him in agony had it landed on his head shocked him back to action more effectively than the serpent's attack. He stood, remembering of course to pull Kuro up by the hand.

lines.jp: その梁材を皮切りに、木造家屋の崩壊が始まった。ノアの言を信ずるなら、これら木造の建物はなまなかな腐食や衝撃などものともしないはずである。それが、朔屋達が立ち上がった、その位置にもごん、と角材を零し、もう連鎖的に降り注ぐ、構造的に弱い芯でもあってそこを射貫かれたのか、それとも飛来した衝撃がそこまでの威力を秘めていたのか。なんにしても、直撃でこそなかったものの、それが大海蛇には致命となった。
lines.en: That beam marked the beginning of the buildings' collapse. If Noah was to be believed, these wooden structures could withstand ordinary decay and impact without difficulty. Yet another squared timber crashed down where Naomasa and Kuro had just risen, followed by a chain of debris. Had some structurally vulnerable core been pierced, or had the incoming blow truly carried that much force? Whatever the reason, though it had not struck the serpent directly, the collapse proved fatal to it.

lines.jp:
朔屋達を外して降った材木は、大海蛇に対しては破砕され、ぎざぎざと出来損ないの、しかし却ってひどい傷を残す槍のように降り注ぎ、その粘膜に覆われた肌に、垂直に突き立ったのだ。大概の打撃や斬撃なら、肌を覆う粘膜が逸らすか絡め取るかでこの生き物に大きな傷を与えるまでには至らない。
　しかしこの時、刀の用法で言えば『刃筋が立った』状態で、角材、柱材、梁材が次々と大海蛇に降り注いで、これには天然の防御膜も抗しようがなかった。
　偶然、といえばもちろん偶然。しかしそう言い切れないほどの執拗さがあった。
　まるで、木造の建築物群が、鬱憤を晴らしているかのように。
lines.en:
The timbers that missed Naomasa and Kuro shattered against the great sea serpent, raining down like crude, jagged spears made all the more damaging by their roughness. They drove vertically into its mucus-covered skin. Most blows or cuts would have been deflected or entangled by that slimy coating before inflicting serious injury. 
But now, in the terminology of swordsmanship, the "edge was aligned." Square timbers, pillars, and beams fell one after another upon the serpent, and even its natural protective membrane could not resist. 
Of course it could be called coincidence. Yet the attack was too relentless to dismiss so easily. 
It was as though the wooden buildings themselves were venting their resentment.

lines.jp: 人間の生などとは時間感覚からして異なる時間を生き延びてきた大海蛇にしても、感じた事のない苦痛、苦痛など知らなかった生き物に、これは生命に関わる危険との警告を乱打する。筋肉が締まる、躍動する、しかしもはや獲物を追い詰めるより、苦痛に反射しての狂乱の踊り、蛇体が呪術に用いる文字のように妖しい曲線を様々に描いて、悶える、仰け反る、丸まる、収縮する、訳も分からず逃げ出す朔屋達の背後で。
lines.en: The great sea serpent had survived through an order of time utterly unlike a human life, yet it had never felt pain like this. To a creature that knew nothing of pain, the sensation hammered out a warning of mortal danger. Its muscles tightened and surged, but no longer in pursuit of prey. It danced in reflexive frenzy, its serpentine body drawing uncanny curves like characters used in sorcery. It writhed, arched, coiled, and contracted behind the fleeing Naomasa and Kuro.

lines.jp:
電撃が走る、幾度も走る、紫煙が立ち籠める。だがもはや、撃たれて喪神する獲物もなく、断末魔の足掻きとして。大海蛇の苦悶にあがく体は、次々に周囲の建物を倒壊させ、より深くそして建材の破砕の尖りでもって悠久を生き抜いた生命を埋めていく。
　最後に、瓦礫の隙間から閃光さえ迸るほどの強烈な放電を放ったが、それこそ最期の吐息、最期の放電に、オゾン臭帯びた煙が立ちのぼる。
lines.en:
Electricity flashed again and again, filling the air with violet smoke. But there was no prey left to stun; these were merely its death throes. The serpent's agonized struggles brought surrounding buildings down one after another, burying the ancient life more deeply beneath the sharp wreckage of their timbers. 
At last, it released a discharge so fierce that light burst from the gaps in the rubble. That was its final breath, its final bolt. Smoke carrying the smell of ozone rose into the air.

lines.jp: 何故生き延びられたのか、喜びよりも不可解さが優るほどの突発的活あり得ない事態に、何とも間の抜けた顔で振り返る二人には、倒壊が大海蛇を狙って殺到しているようにしか見えなかった。安全圏まで離れてみると、排球の試合の様子を見るようにその様がよく判る。流れてきたオゾンの煙に顔をしかめ、見交わす二人の目には、放心の色すら合った。
lines.en: The two turned back with absurdly vacant faces. The sudden, impossible event was so bewildering that confusion outweighed even joy at their survival. To them, the collapse appeared to be deliberately converging on the great sea serpent. Once they reached a safe distance, they could see the whole spectacle clearly, almost like watching a volleyball match. They grimaced at the drifting ozone smoke and exchanged utterly dazed looks.

lines.jp: 劫初の恐怖はかくして絶える───
lines.en: Thus did the primordial terror perish--

lines.jp: 一方、朔屋とクロの、大海蛇との邂逅点から廃屋の家並みを幾重にも隔たった、環礁内の桟橋に停泊した信天翁号の上甲板の上では。
lines.en: Meanwhile, many rows of abandoned buildings away from the place where Naomasa and Kuro encountered the serpent, upon the upper deck of the Albatross moored at the pier inside the atoll...

lines.jp:
バラックの一つの横壁に、大穴が穿たれていた。羆が怒りに任せて突進したのではないかと疑わしい程の穴だが、しかしただの剛力では、穴を穿つ前にこんな組みが荒いバラックなど全体を崩落させるだろう。
　つまりよほどの瞬発的で指向性を有した力が板壁をぶち抜いたと見るべきだが、穴の縁の痕跡を鑑みるに、どうやらその威力は内側から放たれたとしか考えられず。
lines.en:
A large hole had been punched through the side wall of one shack. It was big enough to suggest a brown bear had charged through in a rage, but ordinary brute force would have collapsed such a poorly assembled shack before opening a hole in it. 
The planks must instead have been pierced by an extraordinarily sudden, directional force. And judging from the traces around the opening, that force could only have come from within.

lines.jp: と───ひょいと穴の内側から突き出されて、きょろきょろと辺りの人気を忍ぶように見回したは、とんと巣籠もりの黒貂が時季外れの餌探しに出る風情であったが、大小無数の木屑と埃を浴びて、それでもなお黒耀の艶失わぬ髪の、頭の一揺すりで汚れを振るい落とす、密航者の。
lines.en: A head popped through the hole and glanced around cautiously for witnesses, much like a sable leaving its nest to forage out of season. It belonged to the stowaway. Countless splinters and dust covered her hair, yet its obsidian luster remained. One shake of her head scattered the dirt.

lines.jp: 大海蛇に礫代わりに投げつけられて、いかがわしいレビューの、潤滑液塗されて桃色の光の下でぬらぬら肢体をくねらす踊り子嬢よろしくのたうっていた筈だが一体いつの間にここに、そして衣服にも肌にも粘液の名残もない、その謎の解明は後世に委ねずばなるまい。
lines.en: She had supposedly been thrown at the great sea serpent like a stone and left writhing under its slime in a lurid spectacle. How had she come here, and why was no trace of mucus left on either clothes or skin? The solution to that mystery would have to be entrusted to future generations.

lines.jp:
それより問題なのは、バラックの穴の縁を跨ぎ越した彼女の身のこなしが、周囲に人目のない事を確認してから、悠然としているのに無駄な力みの一切無い自然体となっていたこと。そして、けほ、と小さく優雅に漏らした咳や、髪の間に火薬の匂いを残していたこと。
　つまりはバラックに大穴穿った事態に、彼女の関与があったのは国語事典で『暗躍』の項を引くように明らかであり───
lines.en:
More important was the change in how she moved after stepping over the ragged edge of the hole and confirming no one was nearby. Her posture became relaxed yet perfectly natural, without a trace of wasted tension. Then she gave a small, elegant cough, and the scent of gunpowder lingered in her hair. 
In other words, her involvement in opening the great hole was as obvious as looking up "covert activity" in a dictionary--

lines.jp:
「……一発、つい撃っちゃった。
　ばれないよう、さてなんて誤魔化そう。
　やれやれ……」
lines.en:
...I couldn't resist firing one shot. 
Now, how will I explain it without being found out? 
Good grief...

lines.jp:
どうやら彼女には好ましくない成り行きと見えたが、僅かに吊り上げた唇の形は弦月の秀麗、困じいってるくせに興がる機嫌が揺曳し、あるいは彼女の冴えた眸には。
　朔屋の窮地が映っていたのかも知れない。
lines.en:
The outcome was apparently inconvenient for her, yet the slight curve of her lips made an elegant crescent moon. Even in difficulty, amusement played through her mood. Perhaps her keen eyes had somehow reflected Naomasa's peril.
 Perhaps she had seen it.

lines.jp:
が、余裕はそこまで。
　ぱたり、と、背後に鳴った軽く乾いた響きに怪訝に振り返れば、バラックの壁板の一枚が倒れたところ。
　その一枚が引き金となって残りの壁も四方順繰りにぱたぱたぱたり、支えを失った癖して澄ましかえってボロ屋根が宙に留まっていたが、密航者の注視に今さら気づいたように慌てて落ちる間抜けもの。
lines.en:
But her composure lasted only that long. 
A light, dry slap sounded behind her. She turned suspiciously and saw one plank of the shack's wall lying flat. 
That single board became the trigger: the remaining walls toppled one after another in all four directions. Though deprived of every support, the shabby roof remained suspended in the air with absurd dignity. Then, as if belatedly noticing the stowaway's stare, it hurriedly fell.

lines.jp: だが密航者の眉が引き攣ったのは、壁板と屋根が披露したお座敷芸を不興じたのではなく、バラックという覆いが取り払われて、内部に鎮座していたものが露わになってしまったからである。
lines.en: The stowaway's brows twitched not because the walls and roof had put on an unamusing parlor trick, but because removing the shack's covering exposed what had sat enthroned within.

lines.jp: ごつごつとして、無闇矢鱈と目方があって、角張った鉄塊を積み重ねて、そして筒先をいまだ撃発の余熱でちりちりと空気焦がしている。旧式の。発射に耐えたのが不思議なくらい古めかしい。あわあわと隠しにかかろうにも、偽装していたバラックは屑拾いでも敬遠しそうな廃材に成り果てた。
lines.en: It was rough, impossibly heavy, and assembled from stacked, angular masses of iron. Heat left by the recent shot still scorched the air around the mouth of its barrel. It was an antique, so old-fashioned that surviving the discharge seemed miraculous. Even if she scrambled to conceal it, the shack used as camouflage had become debris that even a scrap collector would reject.

lines.jp: ───バラックの中に収められていたもの。
lines.en: --The object housed inside the shack...

lines.jp: 単装の、艦上砲だった。
lines.en: was a single-barreled deck gun.

lines.jp: ……そして朔屋とクロは。最期、という瞬間に廃屋群を破壊し、大海蛇を瓦礫の中に埋めつくして、二人の生命を救ったあの大轟音は何がもたらしたものか、さっぱり訳がわからなかったけれど、今はそれを詮索するよりもやるべき事がある。
lines.en: ...As for Naomasa and Kuro, they had no idea what caused the tremendous roar that destroyed the abandoned buildings, buried the serpent under rubble, and saved their lives at the very last moment. But for now, they had something more important to do than investigate.

lines.jp:
泪に教えられた通りの道を辿る───
　
　───と。
　廃址の街並みの、小箱を乱雑に重ねたように積層して高さも統一されず段々の中、分けて小高い建物上に塔屋が見える、あれだ。
　もう大海蛇はいない。絶縁のためと着こんだスーツは動きづらく、そして蒸し暑い。二人は建物に入りこんでスーツを脱いでから、塔屋へと続く階段を登り始める。
lines.en:
They followed the route Rui had described--

--and then saw it. 
The buildings of the ruins rose at uneven heights like small boxes carelessly stacked in layers. A tower stood upon one structure taller than the rest. That was their destination. 
The great sea serpent was gone. The insulating suits were hard to move in and oppressively hot. They entered the building, removed the suits, and began climbing the stairs to the tower room.

lines.jp: 足の生えた鰻用か、と怪しいくらい細く長く暗い木の段を三度ほど折り返して上がった建物の屋上、そこもまた板張りの広場で、細雨に侘びしく濡れている、その向こうに小屋掛けされた塔屋が一つ。
lines.en: The dark wooden staircase was so long and narrow that one wondered whether it had been built for eels with legs. After three switchbacks it emerged onto the building's rooftop, another planked square lying desolately beneath the fine rain. Across it stood a single small tower room beneath a roof.

lines.jp: その小さな塔屋に、朔屋とクロもまた、泪が感じたのと同じように、古い時代の船に設けられた船尾楼のような、と言う印象を受けた。
lines.en: The small tower gave Naomasa and Kuro the same impression it had given Rui: it resembled the sterncastle of a ship from an ancient age.

lines.jp:
『我造りし人を我地の面より拭い去らん
　人より獣　天空の鳥に至るまで滅ぼさん
　そは我これを創りしことを悔ゆればなり
　今七日ありて我四〇日四〇夜
　地に雨を降らしめ
　我創りたるあらゆるものを
　地の面より拭い去らん
　かくて七日の後洪水地に臨めり
　その日大淵の源皆潰れ
　雨四〇日四〇夜地に注ぎ
　方舟は水の面に漂えり　　　　　　　　』
lines.en:
"I will wipe from the face of the earth the human race I have created, 
and with them the animals and the birds in the sky, 
for I regret that I have made them. 
Seven days from now I will send rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, 
and I will wipe from the face of the earth 
every living creature 
I have made. 
And after seven days the floodwaters came upon the earth. 
On that day all the springs of the great deep burst forth, 
and rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights. 
The ark floated upon the face of the waters."

lines.jp:
『地に動く肉なるものの鳥　家畜　獣
　地に這う全てのもの　および　人皆死ねり
　その鼻に生命の息の通うもの皆死ねり
　ただ彼と共に
　方舟にありしもののみ残れり
　彼地の面より水の引きしかを見んとて
　鳥を放ちいだしけるが
　再び彼のところへ還らざりき……　　　』
lines.en:
"Every creature that moved upon the earth perished--birds, livestock, wild animals, 
all creatures that swarm upon the earth, and all mankind. 
Everything whose nostrils held the breath of life died. 
Only he remained, 
and those with him in the ark. 
And he sent forth a bird to see whether the waters had receded from the face of the ground, 
but it did not return to him again..."

lines.jp:
屋上を塔屋へと渡る中、小糠雨を渦巻かせて聞こえてきた声、夜毎に島から響いてクロを怯えさせた声。今、その塔屋の中か。
　クロはもうその声を聞いても、ただただ哀しげに唇を噛むばかりで、取り乱したりはしなかったけれど。
　朔屋にはクロが声も涙も見せず、慟哭しているようにしか思われなかったのである。
lines.en:
As they crossed the roof toward the tower, a voice reached them through the swirling drizzle--the voice that had sounded from the island each night and terrified Kuro. Now it came from inside the tower. 
Even upon hearing it, Kuro merely bit her lip in sorrow and did not lose control. 
But to Naomasa, she seemed to be wailing without sound or tears.

lines.jp: 塔屋の扉を開けようとしたのだが、生憎鍵が掛かっていて、朔屋をげんなりさせたけれど、クロが試すと、彼女ならばよし、と許可するようにすんなり開く───この一事を取っても、少女とこの島の繋がりを朔屋に感じさせた。
lines.en: He tried the tower door, but unfortunately it was locked, leaving him dejected. When Kuro tried, however, it opened easily, as if granting her permission. That fact alone made Naomasa feel the girl's connection to the island.

lines.jp: 塔屋内には調度の少なく、書き物机が一脚とそれから───床に点々散っている、これは、鳩の羽根だろうか、そして中に一枚だけ黒いのは、烏の風切り羽根。
lines.en: There was little furniture inside the tower room: a single writing desk, and then... feathers scattered across the floor. Dove feathers, perhaps. Among them lay one black feather, a raven's flight feather.

lines.jp: クロは───その羽根を拾い上げて、胸にかき抱き、涙を一粒、二粒、けれど零したのはそれだけ。後はきっと振りきって、窓の側に座る、一体の人の白骨に向けた。室内に踏みこんだ時から目についてはいた、その白骨。
lines.en: Kuro picked up the feather and clasped it to her chest. One tear fell, then a second, but that was all. She must have forced the rest behind her, for she turned next toward the human skeleton seated beside the window--the skeleton that had caught their eyes from the instant they entered.

lines.jp:
簡素な麻の長衣まとい、小さな椅子に腰かけ、片手を窓枠に差し掛ける形に硬化していた。渇望の形に。
　ノアの妻であったという、この白骨の事、気にならないでもない。
lines.en:
Clad in a simple linen robe, it sat upon a small chair, hardened with one hand reaching toward the window frame--a posture of longing. 
Naomasa could not help wondering about the skeleton said to have been Noah's wife.

lines.jp: 朔屋は書き物机に歩み寄り、机の上に乗せられていた一枚の紙葉に手を伸ばして、そこでクロに振り返る。少女が頷いて促したのに取りあげる、多少黄ばんではいるものの、室内に剥き出しに放置されてきた割りには状態が良い、それがノアの海図だった───どれだけ古いのか定かならぬが、その描線は朔屋が知る現代の海図と遜色ないくらいに精緻を極めていた。
lines.en: Naomasa approached the writing desk and reached toward the sheet of paper lying upon it, then glanced back at Kuro. She nodded for him to continue, so he lifted it. The paper was slightly yellowed, but remarkably well preserved for something left exposed inside the room. This was Noah's sea chart. However old it might be, its lines were as exquisitely precise as any modern chart Naomasa knew.

lines.jp: ───かくして二人はノアの海図を手に入れて、塔屋を後にする。
lines.en: --Thus the two obtained Noah's sea chart and left the tower room.

lines.jp: ───室内には、蔓植物が幾列にも垂れさがり、樹液を滴らせ熱帯性の帷となし、荒原の稲科の草々が風紋にうねり、清いせせらぎが山林の羊歯植物の合間を流れて、砂丘が砂粒の面を陽光に灼かれ星の雫に凍える。ありとあらゆる自然の相が混在し、重なり合い、幾重も幾重も、薄さと立体を兼ね備えた不思議な幕がうねり、波うつ。ありとあらゆる生き物達があった。馴染み深きもの、珍かなもの、異様なもの、強きもの、弱きもの、喰らうもの、喰らわれるもの、古きもの、新しきもの───
lines.en: --Vines hung in row upon row, dripping sap to form tropical curtains. Prairie grasses rolled in wind-shaped patterns. A clear stream ran among mountain ferns, while dunes baked beneath sunlight and froze beneath drops of starlight. Every aspect of nature mingled, overlapped, and folded again and again into strange veils at once thin and deep, billowing in waves. Every manner of living creature was there: familiar and rare, bizarre, strong and weak, devourer and devoured, ancient and new--

lines.jp: 兎が耳を欹てて森のざわめきに聞き入り、獅子が風に向かい鬣をそよがせ、篦鹿の扁平に尖った角が沼沢地から水草をまとわりつかせ浮き上がり、群れを為した狼達が雪煙を巻き上げて駆け抜ける、鼻行類がその粘ついた鼻先に蝿を吸いつけ、翼広げた鷹の影が荒原の低木の上をよぎり、泥沢地の泥の上で蟒蛇が陽差しに血を温める、熊が仔供たちのじゃれ合いを見守りながらのんびりと杉の樹皮に背の毛皮を擦りつけ、畢方がくわえ持ち来たった火によって一つの山林が焼かれ、川獺は河原に獲ってきた魚たちを祭の供物のように並べ、岩塩を求めて象たちは列をなして荒野を渡っていく、原生林の雨に毛並みに雫を宿して雲豹は縄張りを巡回中、角兎の老いた一体が遠く離れた故郷を思う……。
lines.en: A rabbit pricked its ears to the murmuring forest. A lion turned into the wind, mane stirring. The broad, pointed antlers of a moose rose from the marsh trailing water plants. A wolf pack raced through clouds of snow. A snouter caught a fly upon its sticky nose. The shadow of a hawk with wings spread crossed the scrub of a plain. A python warmed its blood in the sun upon marsh mud. A bear lazily rubbed its back against cedar bark while watching its cubs play. Fire carried by a Bifang burned a forest. An otter arranged its caught fish upon a riverbank like offerings for a festival. Elephants crossed a wasteland in single file in search of salt. A clouded leopard patrolled its territory through rain in a primeval forest, droplets caught in its fur. An old horned rabbit remembered its distant homeland...

lines.jp: これらの獣類の中を経巡る老人は、その時代から老人ではあったけれど、当時の慈愛に満ちたその顔相と言ったら、乾いた地に降り注ぐ雨であり、餓えた腹を癒す白く柔らかな麺麭であり、誰もが疲れた足を休める大樹の木陰であり。
lines.en: The old man who wandered among these beasts had already been old in that age. Yet the loving kindness of his face was rain falling upon dry land, soft white bread soothing an empty belly, and the shade of a great tree where anyone might rest tired feet.

lines.jp: 獣類たちは老人を当然のように共同体の中に客人として受け入れ、仔達を眺める事を許したし、牙や爪持つ者たちも風変わりな隣人として日光浴を供にした。全てが調和の中にあり、獣草合い唱和し、神天にしろしめし蝸牛枝に這いなべてこの世は事もなし───けれど、永遠かに見えた自然の平穏は朔屋とクロの眺めるうちにも、失われていったのだった。
lines.en: The animals accepted the old man naturally as a guest within their community and permitted him to watch their young. Even those with fangs and claws shared the sunlight with him as an eccentric neighbor. All things existed in harmony; beast and grass sang together, God reigned in heaven, the snail climbed the branch, and all was right with the world. Yet as Naomasa and Kuro watched, that peace of nature, seemingly eternal, began to disappear.

lines.jp: 滅びの相もまた様々な形態を取っていた。それは戦争（朔屋が知るような、またあるいは全く知らざる戦争もあったし）、疫病が爆発的に蔓延したせいもあった。原因不明の出生率低下が全ての生命体を見舞った事さえある。垂れ流される廃液と煤煙によって地と水が毒され、獣類が生きられなくなった世もあった。そしてもちろん神話・聖典通りに巨大洪水によって地が覆われた事も。
lines.en: Destruction took many forms. There were wars--some Naomasa knew, and others wholly unfamiliar--and explosive epidemics. Once, an unexplained collapse in birthrates afflicted every living thing. In another world, uncontrolled wastewater and smoke poisoned land and water until animals could no longer live. And of course, as myth and scripture described, there were times when a great flood covered the earth.

lines.jp: 老人が経験したのはいかなる滅びだったのだろうか。それは語られず、ただ獣達が。倒れ、落ち、地に伏し、水に沈み、燃えて、老人がどれだけ苦闘しようとも救いきれず、差し延べた手が届く前に死したる屍となり、肉が腐り皮が破け腸が流れ出し───
lines.en: What kind of destruction had the old man experienced? The vision did not say. Animals simply fell, dropped from the sky, collapsed upon earth, sank beneath water, and burned. No matter how he struggled, the old man could not save them all. Before his outstretched hands could reach them, they became corpses. Flesh decayed, skin split, and entrails spilled--

lines.jp:
そして、骨だけを遺した。
　それでも多くの獣達がその船に集められた。実際に野に跳ねていた生き物達を乗船させた事もあったし、大山椒魚だって今回は乗せてもらえて洪水以前の人扱いされずにすんだし、あるいは遺伝子情報のみが集積せられた物もあった。
lines.en:
Only bones remained. 
Even so, many animals were gathered aboard the vessel. Some living creatures that had bounded through the wild were taken aboard directly; this time even the giant salamander was admitted rather than being treated as one of the antediluvians. In other cases, only genetic information was collected.

lines.jp: ───滅びゆく動物達の幻影。老人を取り巻いて。老人は縋ろうとするのだが、幻影達は遠ざかり、薄れぼやけ、消えていくばかり。
lines.en: --Phantoms of the perishing animals surrounded the old man. He tried to cling to them, but they only withdrew, faded, blurred, and vanished.

lines.jp: 扉を開けた途端に眼前に展開された数々の情景に、朔屋とクロは瞬きどころか息をするのも躊躇われ、見入っていたのは暫時の事だったけれども、その僅かな間に歴史を廻り灯籠の画のように何周も繰り返し見たような錯覚に囚われた。
lines.en: The moment they opened the door, countless scenes unfolded before Naomasa and Kuro. For a while they stared, hesitant even to blink or breathe. Yet within that brief span, they felt as if they had watched history circle past again and again like pictures upon a revolving lantern.

lines.jp: 幻影、幻覚の類かそれとも老人の記憶が外界に投影せられたものなのか、いずれ朔屋達は知れず、情景の重ね幕が薄れていけば消え残ったものは、やはりがらんと室内と老人───ノアと、そして島内に遍在する骨の山。
lines.en: Were they illusions, hallucinations, or memories from the old man projected into the outside world? Naomasa and Kuro could not know. As the layered curtains of scenery thinned, what remained was once again only the empty room, the old man Noah, and the mountains of bones spread throughout the island.

lines.jp:
あの情景が何を意味するものか朔屋には判然としなかったけれど、消え果ててみると屋内の淋しさはひたひたと満ち潮のように迫る。
　……別の意味で。
lines.en:
Naomasa could not clearly understand what the vision meant. But once it vanished, the loneliness of the room approached like a steadily rising tide. 
...In another sense as well.

lines.jp: 「……あの、他のみんなは？」
lines.en: ...Um, where is everyone else?

lines.jp: 朔屋達を送り出すだけ送り出しておいて、信天翁号の船員達、室内に一人も見えず。ノアだけが空間に投影された情景の中に佇んでいたのだった。
lines.en: The crew of the Albatross had sent Naomasa and Kuro out, yet now not one of them remained in the room. Only Noah had stood among the scenes projected through the air.

lines.jp: 「……あ。あいつらか？　えーとな、あいつらなら、そのあれだ。船の出港準備をせにゃならんので、先に行くと……」
lines.en: ...Ah. Them? Well, they said they had to prepare the ship to depart, so they went on ahead...

lines.jp:
「……いや、いいよ爺さん、
　そういういらん気遣いはさ。
　みんな、あの淫獣がくたばったところ見て、
　さっさと出てったんだろ……？」
lines.en:
...It's fine, old man. 
You don't need to spare my feelings. 
They saw the obscene beast die 
and hurried out without us, didn't they...?

lines.jp: 朔屋は、問いかけたものの、どうせ答えは判りきっていた事だから、しまいには語尾からして湿気らせ項垂れた。
lines.en: Naomasa had asked, but he knew the answer already. By the end, even the tail of his sentence had gone damp and drooped with his head.

lines.jp:
「ああと……そうとも言う。
　って知るか儂がそんな事、
　大体なんのＱシップかあの砲撃は。
　もうちっとヤツと組んず解れつ、
　粘液と電撃の宴
　見せてくれるかと思うたによ」
lines.en:
Well... that is one way of putting it. 
As if I care about such things! 
And what in blazes was that surprise gunship bombardment? 
I thought you two would wrestle with it a little longer 
and show me a proper feast 
of slime and electricity.

lines.jp:
「はへ……？　やっぱあれ、砲撃だったんか。
　しかしどっから……。
　でもまあ、いいやそんな事は───」
lines.en:
Huh...? So that really was artillery. 
But where did it come from...? 
Well, never mind that--

lines.jp: 実際朔屋の悄気た様と言ったら、クロなどもがらんとした室内におおよその状況を見てとったようだが、放置されたのは同じ彼女にしても、青年に何をどう言ってやればいいのか言葉につまったほど。
lines.en: Naomasa looked so dejected that even Kuro seemed to understand the situation from the empty room. Though she too had been abandoned, she could find no words to say to him.

lines.jp: 「ああ確かにどうでもええわ。お前があんまりしょっぱい顔しとるんでほだされた儂が馬鹿だったわ。お前ら二人とも要らん子扱いだったと言う事だ。あー情けない情けない」
lines.en: Indeed, it does not matter. I was a fool to soften because you looked so pathetic. Both of you were treated like unwanted children. How pitiful. Truly pitiful.

lines.jp: 「うわあ……爺が人の弱味見るとこれだ。なんだよ爺さんあんただって。さっきは部屋ン中にあんな動物ドキュメンタリーおっぴろげて。ついしんみりしそうになったのはこっちだっつーの」
lines.en: Wow... The moment you see somebody's weakness, you go straight for it. What about you, old man? You were just projecting that whole animal documentary across the room. I'm the one who nearly got sentimental.

lines.jp: 少しばかり共感めいた物を覗かせたところで、所詮怪老人は怪老人にしか過ぎず、朔屋の気弱と見ればたちまち居丈高、鶏冠逆立てて猛る老鶏より始末が悪くて、つい同じ土俵で剣突返してしまい、睨み合う、頭巾の奥で陰険に燃える炎と、酒に白目黄ばんだ不摂生の眼差しと。
lines.en: The moment Noah displayed the slightest hint of empathy, he proved himself merely a strange old man after all. At the sight of Naomasa's weakness, he instantly grew overbearing, more troublesome than an enraged old rooster with its comb standing upright. Naomasa responded on his own level, and the two glared at one another: malicious fire burning beneath a hood against an unhealthy gaze with whites yellowed by liquor.

lines.jp: その下から、おろおろと二者を見上げるのが不健康そうな白子の赤の眸で、視殺戦というにしても、なんとも垢抜けない取り合わせではある。
lines.en: Below them, Kuro's unhealthy red eyes looked anxiously from one to the other. As a contest of murderous stares, it was a remarkably unfashionable arrangement.

lines.jp: 先に付き合いきれなくなったのは、ノアだった。
lines.en: Noah was the first to tire of it.

lines.jp:
「うるさいなこちゃこちゃと。最早どうでもええんだそんな事は！
　そんな事より持ってきたんだろうな、海図を」
lines.en:
Enough of your prattle. None of that matters anymore! 
More importantly, you brought the sea chart, did you not?

lines.jp: 乗りだして、迫る老人の、長衣がばさばさ不穏な雲のよう、クロややたじろいで後退り、朔屋の服の裾掴んで、片手の海図を胸にかいこむ。物言いたげな顔で見あげてくる彼女を、力づけてやるように頷き返した。
lines.en: The old man leaned forward, his robe flapping like an ominous cloud. Kuro flinched and stepped back, gripping the hem of Naomasa's clothes while hugging the chart against her chest with one hand. She looked up as if wanting to speak, and he nodded back to encourage her.

lines.jp:
「おう、それだ、それよ……。
　儂の大事な大事な、海図だ」
lines.en:
Yes, that is it... 
My precious, precious sea chart.

lines.jp:
「さあ、の、鴉よ。
　お前が陸地を見つけたというのなら、
　今こそ儂に告げるがよい」
lines.en:
Now then, raven. 
If you truly found dry land, 
this is the time to tell me.

lines.jp:
「その位置、その針路。
　海図に書き入れた時、
　ようやく我が長きにわたる航海も。
　───成就、しようぞ」
lines.en:
Its position and the course toward it. 
When you mark them upon the chart, 
my long voyage will at last... 
--be fulfilled.

lines.jp:
そこまでの生々しい執着を見せているのに、猫撫で声、なんとかしてクロを懐柔しようとしているのが浅ましい、力ずくで奪ったところで海図だけでは無意味なのだろう。
　自分のなりが怯えさせる事を承知はしているのか、触れ得るような間合い以上までは踏みこんでは来ないけれどそれでも、クロの恐れること限りなく、この老人に呪われた夜の事、記憶自体は既に定かではないにしても、よほど忌まわしい感触が骨身に染み着いてしまっているのだろう。
lines.en:
For all the naked obsession he displayed, he used a coaxing voice, shamelessly trying to win Kuro over. Evidently, taking the chart by force would be meaningless without her. 
Perhaps he understood that his appearance frightened her, for he did not step close enough to touch. Even so, Kuro's fear was boundless. Though her memory of the night he cursed her was no longer clear, its loathsome sensation must have soaked into her very bones.

lines.jp:
「なあ、鴉よ。
　早う、な？　何時までもその呪われた姿でいるのは、辛かろう？」
lines.en:
Come now, raven. 
Hurry. It must be painful to remain trapped forever in that accursed form.

lines.jp:
「告げるだけでよいのだ。
　さすればお前は、
　あの賢く、力強き羽根の、
　黒く艶やかな姿に戻れる───」
lines.en:
You need only tell me. 
Then you may return 
to that glossy black form, 
with its wise and powerful wings--

lines.jp:
滴る脂のように妄執をぎらつかせ、迫るノアの猫撫で声は、大洪水から生命の種を守り、次代へと伝えんとした長命人の誇りも気高さも毛ほども感じられず───
　朔屋にはただただ厭うしく、呪わしかった。
　これでは呪われているのは一体どちらなのか、判ったものではない。
lines.en:
Noah's coaxing voice approached, glistening with obsession like dripping grease. It held not a trace of the pride or nobility of a long-lived man who had protected the seeds of life from the great flood and sought to carry them into the next age. 
To Naomasa, it was simply hateful and accursed. 
He could no longer tell which one of them was truly under a curse.

lines.jp:
「戻りたくないか？　本当の姿に。
　戻りたくないか？　空を舞う鴉に」
lines.en:
Do you not wish to return to your true form? 
Do you not wish to become a raven soaring through the sky once more?

lines.jp: 「飛翔するお前は、それは美事なもんだったぞ……風切り羽根を一杯に広げ、鷹にも負けぬ威風であった……」
lines.en: You were magnificent in flight... Your flight feathers spread to their full span, your bearing the equal of any hawk...

lines.jp: 「……今でこそ、そんななりになっておるがな、くく……」
lines.en: ...Though now you have been reduced to that shape. Heh heh...

lines.jp: ノアの語る声音には憎悪と尊崇の入り交じって、老人の、かつてのクロに抱きたる複雑な心を覗かせる。
lines.en: Hatred and reverence mingled in Noah's voice, revealing the complicated feelings he had once held toward Kuro.

lines.jp:
クロは、ノアの妄念に、悪臭を嗅いだように海図を抱いたまま後じさったけれど、ノアの黒々とした妄執に記憶の扉こじ開けられたか、ふっと遠くに焦点を置く目になった、それは恐らく空高く飛翔せるものの、高みを往く眼差しなのであったろう。
　───在りし日の、クロの。
lines.en:
Kuro recoiled from Noah's delusion as if smelling something foul, still clutching the chart. But perhaps his black obsession forced open the door to her memories, for her eyes suddenly focused far away. It was likely the gaze of something flying high above, looking down from the heights. 
--Kuro as she had once been.

lines.jp:
「───そうだ。
　クロはほんとは、カラスだったんだ」
lines.en:
--That's right. 
Kuro was really a raven.

lines.jp:
「嵐の中、どこまでも飛んでける。
　どこが陸地なのか、探して、どこまでも」
lines.en:
Kuro could fly anywhere through the storm.
 She searched and searched for dry land, no matter how far she had to go.

lines.jp:
「ずっと昔は、クロは。
　なによりも知恵のある、カラスで。
　他のどの鳥よりも、
　飛ぶのが上手なカラスで」
lines.en:
Long, long ago, Kuro was 
a raven wiser than anything else, 
and better at flying 
than any other bird.

lines.jp: 低く呟くクロは、過去に僅かなりとも触れたせいか、常よりも舌が座って、思慮とさえ言える深い心を感じさせ、なるほど鴉、と朔屋に思わせた。
lines.en: As Kuro murmured quietly, the brief contact with her past seemed to steady her tongue. Her voice held a depth that might even be called thoughtfulness. Yes, Naomasa found himself thinking. A raven indeed.

lines.jp: と言ってクロは、そのひ弱い両手で羽ばたきの真似事などしてみせたのではない。人の姿形で鳥を飛翔を真似ても不様なだけ、クロはただ、一瞬だけ嵐の時の彼女の眸を取り戻しただけ。すぐに曇ってしまったけれど、その鋭き眼力は、あの思慮深き黒き鳥なのだと、なるほどと朔屋を。
lines.en: Kuro did not flap her frail hands in imitation as she spoke. A human shape pretending to be a bird in flight would only look pitiful. For a single instant, she simply regained the eyes she possessed within a storm. They soon clouded again, but that keen gaze convinced Naomasa: this was the thoughtful black bird.

lines.jp:
鴉、鴉、思慮ある鳥よ、いと黒き鳥よ。あらゆる鳥の中でも群を抜いての知恵者よ。神話、伝説中の常連よ。お前達は後代その賢しきが故に時に人から忌み嫌われる事もあったけれど、その出自は輝かしい。その羽根の黒さの由来は、時に太陽とも結びつく。天空の黄金の炎に近づきすぎたために、その羽根黒く焦がされたのだ、とも。
　太陽の隠語として『金烏』と言う語すらあるではないか。
lines.en:
Raven, raven, thoughtful bird, blackest of birds. Wisest by far among all the creatures of the air, a constant figure in myth and legend. In later ages, people sometimes despised ravens for their very cleverness, yet their origin was glorious. The blackness of their feathers was sometimes associated with the sun: they had flown too near its golden fire and been scorched black. 
Was not the expression "golden crow" itself another name for the sun?

lines.jp:
鴉、知恵のある鴉、であるならば、たとえかつての主であったとしても、お前を呪うような相手には、否むがよい。
　───またとあらじ！　と啼いてみせるがよい。
lines.en:
If you are a raven--a wise raven--then refuse the one who cursed you, even if he was once your master.
 Cry out: Never again!

lines.jp:
けれど、クロは。
　否みもせず、眼力で射貫きもせず。
　ただ、哀れな声を───
lines.en:
But Kuro 
neither refused nor pierced him with her gaze. 
She merely spoke in a pitiful voice.

lines.jp: 「それなのにクロは、降りられる陸地を見つけられなかったから」
lines.en: But Kuro couldn't find any dry land where she could land.

lines.jp: ノアが方舟から放ったという鴉は、風雨の中に飛び立っては幾度となく戻ってきたという───陸地を見つけられなかったら、戻ってきたのだという。
lines.en: The raven Noah released from the ark had flown into the wind and rain, then returned again and again. Whenever it failed to find land, it came back.

lines.jp:
「おじいに教えてあげられなかったから。
　でも、そのせいなの？
　クロが今、こんなになっちゃったのは」
lines.en:
Kuro couldn't tell Grandpa where it was. 
But is that why? 
Is that why Kuro became like this?

lines.jp:
クロは、かつて嵐を衝いて舞い上がっていた時代がもしあったとしても、声にも、そのか細い肩にも、手足にも、鳥の中の鳥としての矜持や気概は全く見えず、呪われてあった年月が、彼女に何をもたらしたのか、どう変えてしまったのかを物語っていた。
　震えて舌足らずの言葉、か弱き手足にひ弱な白い肌。何もかもが、かつての彼女が偉大であればあったほど、今の彼女の哀れを酷薄に告げる。
lines.en:
Even if Kuro had once soared against the storm, no pride or spirit worthy of the greatest of birds remained in her voice, her narrow shoulders, or her limbs. The years beneath the curse showed what they had done to her, how completely they had changed her.
 Trembling, halting words; weak limbs and frail white skin. The greater she had once been, the more cruelly every part of her proclaimed her present misery.

lines.jp:
「……待たされすぎたよ、儂らは。
　刻一刻と失われていく生命。
　守るべき物達が失われていく絶望」
lines.en:
...We waited too long. 
Lives vanished with every passing moment. 
The despair of watching everything we were meant to protect disappear.

lines.jp:
「鴉、お前が飛び呆けている間になあ……。
　お前は幾度か船に戻ってきたが。
　お前は何も持ち来たらんかった。
　儂らの希望、約束の地の証を、なにも」
lines.en:
While you went on flying, raven... 
You returned to the ship several times. 
But you never brought us anything. 
No hope, no proof of the promised land. Nothing.

lines.jp:
「その度に深まる我らの絶望───
　お前には判るまいなあ」
lines.en:
Each time, our despair deepened--
but you could never understand that.

lines.jp:
憂愁に深く沈んだ吐息でクロを責めるノアの、恨みの深さは伝わっても、だからと朔屋を納得させるものではない。
　二者の間に進み出たのは、老人の非難がましい視線からクロを遮るために。
lines.en:
Noah blamed Kuro with a sigh sunk deep in sorrow. Naomasa could feel the depth of his resentment, but that did not make it reasonable. 
He stepped between the two to block Kuro from the old man's accusing gaze.

lines.jp:
「爺さん、そりゃあひどいだろう。
　どう考えてもあんたの逆恨みじゃないか」
lines.en:
That's cruel, old man. 
However you look at it, you're blaming her for your own failure.

lines.jp: ───鴉の騎士を気取ったつもりであったとしたならば、朔屋は一言の元に斬って捨てられた。
lines.en: --If Naomasa meant to play the raven's knight, he was cut down in a single stroke.

lines.jp: 「黙れこの少女性愛者。お前な、子供は慈しみ育てる者であって、セックスの対象にするもんじゃないだろうが。その上お前は鳥姦嗜好者じゃ。重度の変態だ」
lines.en: Silence, you pedophile. Children are to be cherished and raised, not made into sexual objects. And on top of that, you lust after birds. You are a hopeless degenerate.

lines.jp: 「お前な、何を気取っているつもりか知らんが、そこのところ、少し顧みたらどうだ？」
lines.en: I do not know what image you are trying to cultivate, but perhaps you should reflect upon that.

lines.jp: ……朔屋は、言葉の針に、しかも返しがついた針に心を深々と抉られて、廃屋の床の上を耳を押さえて転がり廻っていて、クロの盾すら満足にこなせないのだった。
lines.en: ...The barbed needle of his words pierced deep into Naomasa's heart. He rolled across the abandoned house's floor with his hands over his ears, unable even to serve properly as Kuro's shield.

lines.jp: 「だいたいな、逆恨みかどうかなぞ、誰が決めるんだ。怨む本人には、怨めしい怨めしいという思いがあっても、それを不当な恨みとは思うまい」
lines.en: Besides, who decides whether resentment is justified? The one who bears it feels only resentment, resentment, and never considers it unjust.

lines.jp: 「そんな……」
lines.en: That's...

lines.jp:
悲痛な声、今もしクロが涙を零したならば、眸の血の赤が混じって薄赤く滴りそうなくらい、痛切な声。
　ノアの言葉は、人の業の深さを思い知らせ、クロを打ちのめす。
lines.en:
Her voice was so anguished that if Kuro wept now, the blood-red of her eyes seemed ready to mingle with the tears and stain them pale crimson.
 Noah's words forced the depth of human perversity upon her and crushed her beneath it.

lines.jp:
「ひどい、なんでクロだけ……。
　クロばっか、なんで……」
lines.en:
It's cruel. Why only Kuro...? 
Why is it always Kuro...?

lines.jp:
「じゃから、それもここまでだと言うておるのに。さ、早う、な？　……な？
　何を躊躇う？　望んでその哀れな姿に留まろうというのか？」
lines.en:
I am telling you that it may end now. Come, quickly. Well? 
Why hesitate? Do you actually wish to remain in that pitiful shape?

lines.jp: かき口説く老人の、いやらしい声の他に、クロに問いかける声があった。
lines.en: Besides the old man's repulsively coaxing voice, another voice questioned Kuro.

lines.jp:
───じゃあクロよ、お前は。
　
　───どうするつもりなんだ？
lines.en:
--Then what about you, Kuro? 

--What do you intend to do?

lines.jp: ───行ってしまうのか？　元の姿を取り戻して、どこかに飛んで行ってしまうのか？
lines.en: --Will you leave? Regain your original form and fly away somewhere?

lines.jp: ───それに、この爺に陸地を教えたところで、本当にお前の呪いは解かれるのか？
lines.en: --And even if you tell this old man where the land is, will that really break your curse?

lines.jp: ───もし爺さんが約束を守ってくれなけりゃ、お前は今のクロのままだぜ？
lines.en: --If the old man doesn't keep his promise, you'll stay as you are now, Kuro.

lines.jp: ───今のままでも、嵐が来ればお前はすごい奴じゃないかよう。それで、足りないのか、なあ、クロ。
lines.en: --Even as you are, you're incredible whenever a storm comes. Isn't that enough? Tell me, Kuro.

lines.jp:
誰あろう、誰でもない、朔屋の声だった。ノアの糾弾から、ようやく我を取り戻した朔屋だった。いまだノアからの非難の傷は深く、身を起こすのも大儀で、ゆっくり立ち上がり、足許を確かめるように踏みしめて、クロの背後に立つ。
　けれど。後ろから支えてやるような位置に立ちながら、朔屋の言葉はよりクロを迷わせるものでしかない。
　何が青年をして、そのような惑わす言葉を吐かせたものか。
lines.en:
It was no one's voice but Naomasa's. He had finally recovered from Noah's condemnation. The wound left by the accusation remained deep; even sitting up was an effort. He slowly rose, planted each step as if testing the ground, and stood behind Kuro. 
But although he positioned himself as though to support her from behind, his words could only deepen her confusion. 
What made the young man speak in a way that left her so uncertain?

lines.jp:
「いいよ。もう。朔屋さんの好きにして。
　クロはね。もう考えられない」
lines.en:
Fine. Do whatever you want, Sakuya.
 Kuro cannot think anymore.

lines.jp: 「……いいんだな、ほんとに、それで」
lines.en: ...Are you sure? Is that really what you want?

lines.jp: 朔屋にことりと背中を預けて、あいと頷いた、クロの横顔の線には、他者に全てを委ねきって後悔の翳り一つ無く、ただ白々と、白々と。
lines.en: Kuro gently rested her back against Naomasa and nodded yes. The line of her profile held not a shadow of regret at entrusting everything to another. It was only pale, pale white.

lines.jp: 「どのくらい、飛び続けて、こうなったんだろう」
lines.en: How long did Kuro keep flying before she became like this?

lines.jp:
首筋から胸元に流れる髪を一筋、指の中に掬いとる。白くて汚れを吸ったらすぐに目立ち、腰もなく、もつれやすい髪。伸ばしっぱなしの髪。
　何時から───こうなのだろう。
lines.en:
She gathered one strand of hair flowing from her neck across her chest between her fingers. White hair that showed dirt immediately, limp and easily tangled, left to grow without end. 
Since when had it been this way?

lines.jp: 「こうなったその時に、クロはもう、終わってたんだ、きっと。もう、後はつけたしみたいなもの」
lines.en: When Kuro became like this, Kuro's life was probably already over. Everything after that was only an addition.

lines.jp:
髪を掬った、手首も眺める。
　枯れた木の枝のように細くて、やはり白い、肌の薄い手だ。非力で、他の人なら軽々運べるものでも、ちょっと持ち上げただけで疲れてしまう腕。足だってそう。歩くだけなら随分と遠出も出来るけれど、駆け足は下手くそ、すぐに縺れて転んでしまう。
　一体いつから、こうだったのだろう。
lines.en:
She looked at the wrist of the hand holding her hair. 
It was thin as a dead twig and just as white, covered in delicate skin. The arm was so weak that lifting something another person could easily carry soon exhausted it. Her legs were the same. She could walk surprisingly far, but she ran poorly, became tangled in herself, and quickly fell. 
Since when had she been this way?

lines.jp:
「でも、朔屋さんがクロをおんなのこに、
　そしておんなにしてくれた時は、
　うれしかったよ」
lines.en:
But when Sakuya made Kuro a girl,
 and then made her a woman,
 Kuro was happy.

lines.jp: 語りながら、身体を眺め下ろす。痩せこけて、どんなに食べても大きくなれない身体だ。そもそもそんなに沢山は食べられない。何時か誰かに、きっとそのうちに背も伸びるし、そうしたら胸だってふっくらしてくると言われたような気もするけれど、あれは誰だったろう。
lines.en: As she spoke, she looked down over her body. It was thin and could not grow larger no matter how much she ate. She could not eat very much in the first place. She vaguely remembered someone once telling her she would surely grow taller one day, and that her chest would fill out then. Who had it been?

lines.jp:
結局、いつまで経っても自分はこのままだ。
　けれど、こんな髪でも、手足でも、身体でも。
lines.en:
In the end, no matter how much time passed, she remained the same. 
Yet even with this hair, these limbs, and this body...

lines.jp:
馬鹿で、物覚えが悪くて、他の人からはまともに見てもらえない自分でも。
　この人は、自分を抱いてくれた。他の人が近寄らないところまで踏みこんで、他の人がしてくれない事をしてくれて、そして自分に教えてくれた。
lines.en:
Though she was stupid, slow to learn, and never properly seen by anyone else--
this man had held her. He had stepped closer than anyone else would, done what no one else would do, and taught her.

lines.jp:
クロには判らなかった事を、教えてくれた朔屋。
　他の誰でもない、クロの側にいてくれた朔屋。
　そんな朔屋なら───もう、なにもかも。
lines.en:
Naomasa had taught Kuro what she did not understand. 
Naomasa, no one else, had remained by Kuro's side. 
If it was that Naomasa, then she could entrust him with everything.

lines.jp:
委ねてしまっていいのではないかと、クロは。多分、あの大海蛇の前で、この青年となら最期を共にするのも幸せなのだと知ってしまった時から、クロは。
　青年に、自分に遺された、最後の大事な芯を預けてしまっていたのだろう。
lines.en:
Kuro thought she might surrender it all to him. Perhaps from the moment she realized before the serpent that sharing her end with this young man could itself be happiness, 
she had entrusted him with the last precious core remaining within her.

lines.jp:
「何を言うているのだ、お前は……。
　ここまで来て、全てを棄てるつもりか」
lines.en:
What are you saying...? 
Have you come this far only to abandon everything?

lines.jp:
「だまれ───だまれ、おじい。
　この人は、おじいが取っていって全部。
　クロから全部取っていったクロを」
lines.en:
Be quiet--be quiet, Grandpa.
 This man--after Grandpa took everything away.
 After Grandpa took everything from Kuro--

lines.jp:
「抱いてくれた。おじいなんか、呪っただけ。
　おじいなんか、おじいなんか───」
lines.en:
He still held Kuro. Grandpa only ever cursed her.
 Grandpa--Grandpa--

lines.jp:
これまでノアに怯え続けていたクロが、初めて老人に反抗してみせた、顔は歯を剥き出しにして睨みつける、追いつめられた挙げ句の悲壮感ばかりが滲む相ではあったけれど。
　それでも確かに少女はノアに逆らってみせたのだ。屹と目を剥き、拳を握りしめて、きっぱりと告げた。訣別しようとしていた。
lines.en:
Kuro, who had always cowered before Noah, defied the old man for the first time. She bared her teeth and glared, her expression filled less with courage than the desperation of someone driven into a corner. 
Yet the girl had unquestionably resisted him. She opened her eyes wide, clenched her fists, and spoke firmly. She was trying to sever their bond.

lines.jp:
「ここにきて、
　なんにもできなかったくせに。
　朔屋さんみたいな人とも、
　会えなかったくせに」
lines.en:
You came here, 
but you couldn't do anything. 
You never even met someone 
like Sakuya.

lines.jp: 「クロの方が、かってるよ」
lines.en: Kuro wins.

lines.jp:
クロは心を決めつつある今だったが、朔屋はまだ迷いを残していた。
　クロを老人の願いから解放してやるべきなのか、どうか。迷うまでもない事なのだ、とは思う。けれどそれを選んでしまうのは、自分の生をも決定づけてしまうのではないか───
　そんな躊躇いにも囚われたけれど。
　それでも朔屋は───
lines.en:
Kuro was settling upon her choice, but Naomasa still hesitated. 
Should he free her from the old man's wish or not? It seemed there should be no question. Yet making that choice might determine the course of Naomasa's own life as well. 
That uncertainty held him. 
Even so, Naomasa--

lines.jp: 解放してやらない
lines.en: Do not set her free

lines.jp: 解放してやる
lines.en: Set her free
